Children across England can enjoy free bus travel throughout August.

The initiative is designed to alleviate financial pressures on families during the school summer holidays.

The Department for Transport (DfT) confirmed that most under-16s will not be required to pay for travel on the majority of local bus services throughout August.

The DfT identified several popular sites which are accessible via the free travel scheme, such as York Dungeon, Windsor Castle and the National Space Centre in Leicester.

Typically, bus fares for children aged five to 15 range from £1 to £2, while those under five years old already benefit from free bus travel.

open image in gallery Most under-16s will not be required to pay for travel on the majority of local bus services throughout August ( Ian West/PA Wire )

Secretary of state for transport Heidi Alexander said earlier this year: “I know that the cost of living is a concern for households across the UK, which is why we’re cutting the cost of the day-to-day, with free bus travel for children this summer.”

Other measures to ease the cost-of-living burden throughout summer holidays

The government introduced the “Great British Summer Savings” scheme.

Here, VAT has been cut on items such as children’s meals at restaurants, children’s theatre and cinema tickets, and family attractions including theme parks and adventure centres.

Former chancellor Rachel Reeves announced the measure as part of a package aimed at easing the impact on the cost of living from the Iran war.

Peppa Pig World, Alton Towers and Legoland are among the well-known attractions taking part.

Theme parks and cinemas welcomed the slashing of VAT, with British Association of Leisure Parks, Piers and Attractions chief executive Paul Kelly saying it was “a very welcome and timely boost for the UK’s visitor attraction sector”.

open image in gallery Legoland, Peppa Pig World and Alton Towers are among the well-known attractions taking part ( Legoland/PA )

“Our members stand ready to pass on this benefit and deliver brilliant, memorable experiences for visitors of all ages.”

UK Hospitality chair Kate Nicholls said a lower rate of VAT for hospitality was “the quickest and simplest way to lower prices and boost consumer confidence”.

£2 cap on bus fares

Last week, the government announced it will reintroduce a £2 cap on bus fares for all passengers from the start of next year.

The current cap is £3.

Ms Alexander said: “We’re giving families room to breathe from the cost of living squeeze.

“With free bus travel for five to 15-year-olds and discounts on kids’ meals at restaurants, cinema tickets and theme parks, we’re helping people make the most of the time they have together for the school holidays.

“Not only are we lowering costs for the summer, the £2 bus fare cap will help all passengers get to where they need to for less.”

If England needed any reminder of the gap that exists at the top of the netball world, they were served a ruthless reminder by New Zealand in the Commonwealth Games semi-final.

The Silver Ferns brushed past the Roses 61-54 in Glasgow to book a first Commonwealth Games final since 2014 in emphatic fashion, as England’s chances of regaining the title they won in 2018 came to an end.

It was a scoreline that flattered an embattled England, who only briefly looked like being able to truly challenge after a fast start from New Zealand.

England threw away their very first centre pass and it set the tone for the contest in which the Roses were always chasing and were let down by their own errors.

Anna Stembridge’s side fought their way back to within four nearing half time but were then subjected to another New Zealand blitz at the start of the third quarter that effectively won the match.

The score quickly blew out to a double-figure deficit at one stage, and it could easily have stayed that way had New Zealand not taken their foot off the gas in the final quarter.

Defeat to the world’s No.2 side was a fair reflection of where this England side sit in the global pecking order, with New Zealand and gold medal favourites Australia still a cut above the rest. The Diamonds look to be on another level altogether in Glasgow.

Closing that gap has been the perennial challenge for England, but attention first turn to Sunday morning’s bronze medal match, where the Roses will seek to avoid a repeat of the fourth-place finish they endured four years ago.

“I don't want that feeling again,” said goal shooter Eleanor Cardwell, “Going through this four years ago will definitely add extra fuel to the fire. We really want to come away with a medal.

“Obviously bronze isn't what we came here for, but it's what we're fighting for now."

In the cold hard light of day, a bronze medal would represent success for the Roses given the six months they endured in preparation for Glasgow 2026.

open image in gallery Grace Nweke was too much for England to handle in the netball semi-final ( Getty )

The netball world was rocked by the resignation of head coach Jess Thirlby in March, with assistant Stembridge stepping into the breach just four months out from netball’s pinnacle event.

Star player Helen Housby was then ruled out with injury in June, before Beth Cobden and Nat Metcalf were later also sidelined. All three were part of squad that won the historic gold in 2018 and boasted 258 caps between them.

The pre-tournament concern was that England would not even reach the semi-finals and crash out at the pool stage for the first time since the sport was introduced to the Commonwealth Games in 1998.

That alternative apocalypse was avoided with a 58-54 victory over an exciting South Africa side, but New Zealand was always going to pose a far sterner test.

The Silver Ferns are wily operators and have parked their own off-court problems to win all five pool matches before outclassing England.

Kiwi head coach Dame Noeline Taurua was suspended by Netball New Zealand in September 2025 after allegations of bullying but was reinstated in October after significant support from some players.

Taurua is known to be a tough taskmaster and had her side perfectly drilled against the Roses, with the Silver Ferns’ lack of errors and clinical shooting the key differences on Saturday morning.

England opted for the same defence that had changed the game against South Africa, with London Pulse pair Halimat Adio and Funmi Fadoju in from the start but they were unable to shackle Grace Nweke.

open image in gallery England's defeat shows how far they still need to improve to challenge for the top medals ( Getty )

It was not just them, as all England options struggled to stop her or the regular flow of feeds serving her while the Roses found it tough to score freely at the other end.

There will be plenty of time for reflection after Sunday as England work out where to go next with a World Cup less than a year away, but the Roses must first focus on battling for a bronze that they surely would have taken before arriving in Glasgow.

“There's still a chance to win a medal and that's an exciting opportunity,” said Stembridge. “We do not want to leave here without a medal. This team has shown such resilience through so many curveballs, even before the tournament.

“We'll look at what we can take forward from today, what's worked really well for us and what's served us well. Then we'll look at the points of difference of the opposition we're going to face.

“We'll make sure we're fully prepared and throw everything at it tomorrow.”

Thanks to National Lottery players, more than £33m is raised every week for good causes. It’s because of you that sport, arts, heritage, and community projects, as well as our athletes competing at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, are supported across the UK.

Thousands of survivors of Japan’s powerful 6.8-magnitude earthquake have been forced to sleep in cars and crowded makeshift shelters as an intense heatwave grips the country, compounding misery for communities already devastated by the disaster.

The death toll from the earthquake that shook Kumamoto Prefecture in southwestern Japan has risen to 36, while six others remain in serious condition, according to prefectural authorities.

The earthquake and nearly 100 subsequent aftershocks flattened homes, snapped bridges, crumbled roads and triggered an explosion at a shopping mall, sparking a massive search-and-rescue operation.

open image in gallery People take shelter at the ‘Wing Matsubase’ General Sports and Cultural Center in Uki, Kumamoto Prefecture ( AFP/Getty )

More than 1,500 buildings were damaged, including 179 that were destroyed, according to preliminary assessments by Kumamoto officials.

The earthquake forced more than 9,000 people to seek refuge in evacuation shelters, where authorities are working to restore running water and electricity to power air conditioning.

Japan is reeling under punishing summer temperatures, with highs reaching 36C (97F). Japan's weather agency and the ministry of the environment issued an extreme heat alert for Kumamoto City on Friday, raising fears of heatstroke among people left homeless by the quake.

Temperatures are expected to hit 40C on Monday, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency, which has urged people to take precautions.

Fuel has become scarce after power outages knocked petrol stations offline and earthquake damage disrupted deliveries from other regions.

open image in gallery A gas station employee distributes drinks to drivers waiting in line for fuel following the the July 28 earthquake, in Yatsushiro, Kumamoto prefecture ( AFP/Getty )

open image in gallery Cars wait in line for fuel at a gas station following the the July 28 earthquake ( AFP/Getty )

Many evacuees have resorted to sleeping in their cars for privacy, but the shortage has made it difficult to keep the air conditioning running in the scorching heat.

Hirokazu Sato, who lost his home in the earthquake, said he, his wife and their three children would remain in their car until they could move into temporary housing.

"I don't know how soon I'd be able to move in," Sato said. "We need to have the air conditioning on throughout the day and night, which uses up gas."

open image in gallery Vehicles are crushed under collapsed buildings in Yatsushiro ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi stressed that authorities must secure water supplies by doing "whatever it takes" and called for close coordination with the military and other relevant agencies.

Along with fuel, water services have been cut off for 72,000 households in the prefecture, according to Japan Times, with a timeline for restoring service unknown.

Authorities have said they are working to step up efforts to strengthen water supply support, including the dispatch of water trucks to priority locations.

Among those forced to cram into a car was Tomoko Takaoka, a 31-year-old factory worker who was unable to stay at an evacuation shelter with her two dogs.

Faced with the choice of sheltering without her Chihuahua and Chihuahua-poodle mix, Ms Takaoka instead turned to her car to protect herself and her pets from the heat.

open image in gallery Tomoko Takaoka, 31, who evacuated from Uki with her pet dogs Chihuahua Ku (7) and Chihuahua mixed with poodle Sheri (8) ( Reuters )

After coming across social media posts about a veterinary hospital that has converted into a shelter for owners of cats and dogs, she moved to Ryunosuke Animal Hospital in downtown Kumamoto.

The facility is providing separate rooms for canines and felines after learning from the 2016 earthquake in Kumamoto that left almost 280 people dead.

"During disasters, it's only natural for dogs and cats to stay together with their families. But people who don't own pets don't necessarily want to be with them," hospital director Ryunosuke Tokuda said.

"They worry about fleas, odours, allergies and noise. Pets are often viewed negatively, which is why many evacuation shelters don't allow people and pets to stay together," he added.

Ms Takaoka was among 26 evacuees and their pets sheltering at the hospital in tents.

"They're just like family to me. I'd like to stay with them as much as possible," she said.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

The search entered its fifth day on Saturday after the critical 72 hour window – when there is the best chance to reach people alive – ended. Authorities said they are making efforts to locate every unaccounted person and identify those who have been found.

Of the 36 deaths, 27 victims have been identified.

Rescue workers continued to look through the rubble at the Aeon Mall in Kashima town, one of the hardest-hit sites. The complex had some 3,000 shoppers and hundreds of members of staff inside when the earthquake struck. About an hour later an explosion ripped through a part of the mall where some staff members were working, causing the second floor to collapse.

Rescuers pulled 12 people out of the mall with seven confirmed dead and five others injured. Officials did not say if more people were missing at the site.

A search operation has now ended at a Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro city where a chimney collapsed in the quake, officials said. Of the 11 people dug out there, nine were confirmed dead.

News.title: Richarlison earns last-gasp win for 10-man Tottenham against Chelsea
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur 2 Chelsea 1

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.



Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

Sports.title: Uefa declares loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino as it vows to stop ‘shabby back-room’ plots happening again
Sports.content:
UEFA have hit out at Gianni Infantino’s “shabby, backroom” plot to sell off the World Cup and declared a loss of confidence in the despised head of world football.

Fifa president Infantino has come under fire after announcing plans to let private investors buy up a chunk of the global tournament.



There has been a global backlash and Uefa threatened to stage a boycott against future World Cups if Fifa went ahead with it.

But Uefa – led by chief Alexander Ceferin – welcomed news that Fifa had backed down and vowed to make sure a similar plot doesn’t happen again.



And they said they had lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership after the damaging debacle.

The organisation said in a statement: “UEFA welcomes FIFA’s decision to withdraw its plan to sell a stake in its competitions – including the World Cup – into private hands.



“We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

“It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again.

“That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA’s confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.”

It accused Infantino of “failing to deliver” on his vow to provide “transparency” after taking over the role in 2016.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The statement added: “The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through were anything but transparent.

“We must start to use some of that money that is sat idle in FIFA’s bank account to deliver the kick start that the grassroots and the wider game need in each of the 211 countries of FIFA. But we don’t need to sell off the family silver to pay for it.

“This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun.”

Uefa were joined by CONCACAF and the AFC federations in opposing the move, which effectively killed off any hope of it getting through.



UEFA STATEMENT IN FULL UEFA welcomes FIFA’s decision to withdraw its plan to sell a stake in its competitions – including the World Cup – into private hands. The proposal was unanimously rejected by UEFA’s national associations and by many other federations and confederations of all sizes around the world, whose job it is to protect football. UEFA thanks all the fans, leagues, clubs, players, individuals, associations and confederations that opposed the scheme, alongside the many Prime Ministers, Heads of State and commentators who have demonstrated to the FIFA President that football is not for sale. We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account. It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA’s confidence but also that of many other members of the football family. When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA’s Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, “Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA. You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA,” before telling the assembled stakeholders, “The money of FIFA is your money. It’s not the money of the FIFA President. It’s your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.” On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through were anything but transparent. And with reserves standing at over $5bn, he has also failed to use associations’ money for the benefit of the game. UEFA will begin work immediately with partners and stakeholders all over the world and right across the game to propose a new way of distributing resources through the existing FIFA Forward programme. We must start to use some of that money that is sat idle in FIFA’s bank account to deliver the kick start that the grassroots and the wider game need in each of the 211 countries of FIFA. But we don’t need to sell off the family silver to pay for it. This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun.

Fifa wanted to create a subsidiary called Fifa Forward Enterprise, which would have presided over money-making assets at the World Cup.

Football’s governing body valued the branch at £15bn and were hoping to sell a 20 per cent stake for £3.1bn.

But Infantino said he recognised the project had “created divisions” that mean it could no longer move forwards.

He said: “Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place. Our purpose has always been – and will always be – to unite and improve.

“As a result, this proposal will not proceed. Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.”

But he isn’t about to walk away from the top job – even after his senior advisor quit and the whole of Uefa turned on him.

With the challenge of rebuilding trust once again, Infantino faces a huge period ahead after Spain won a controversial final which even featured a half-time show for the first time ever.



Infantino had been well placed to head into a fourth term in charge with no opposition.

However, the controversy has put his 2027 election sweep in serious doubt.

Sports.title: Chelsea avoid massive points deduction as more details emerge on FA transfer ban decision
Sports.content:
Chelsea avoid massive points deduction as more details emerge on FA transfer ban decision

The Football Association sanctioned Chelsea for 74 breaches of rules around agent regulation after their current owners reported and admitted to misconduct by their previous ownership

View 2 Images Chelsea managed to avoid potential relegation by appealing their points deduction (Image: Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Chelsea were initially earmarked for a 15-point deduction for their 74 breaches of football agent regulations. Such a penalty would have relegated the Blues from the Premier League last season.

‌



They only finished 13 points clear of West Ham United in the table, with the starting point for their penalty being enough to leave them two points adrift in 18th place. However, it was reduced by a third, to 10 points, for the London club's cooperation and self-reporting.

‌



Their misconduct occurred during Roman Abramovich's almost two-decade-long ownership. Chelsea's new owners, BlueCo, ultimately successfully appealed against a six-point deduction.

‌



Chelsea hit with £10m fine and suspended transfer ban after Roman Abramovich breaches READ MORE :

How Chelsea managed to escape Premier League points deduction as FA explain charges READ MORE :

On Friday, it was announced that the Blues had been hit with a £10million fine by the FA, alongside a suspended two-window transfer ban. The FA brought charges against Chelsea in September 2025 for conduct 'ranging from 2009 to 2022'.

However, it 'primarily relates to events which occurred between the 2010/11 and 2015/16 playing seasons'. The allegations, which Chelsea contested, centred largely on transfers, including the acquisitions of Eden Hazard, Samuel Eto'o and Willian.

Chelsea's current ownership self-reported the violations that prompted the FA charges. BlueCo are believed to have been fully cooperative with the FA throughout their year-long inquiry.

‌



The FA's written reasons say that, of the club's punishment, "a starting point of 15 points is appropriate". Additional reasoning outlined in the report explains why the recommended points penalty was ultimately lowered.

"'The starting point will accordingly be reduced by 1/3 to 10 points to reflect the general mitigation under the heads of self-reporting and cooperation," the written reasons stated.

View 2 Images Chelsea's charges relate to their business during Roman Abramovich's time at the club (Image: Getty Images)

‌



A statement from the FA read: "A financial sanction of £10 million and a suspended two-window registration ban have been imposed on Chelsea FC for breaches of The Football Association [The FA] Football Agent Regulations, Regulations on Working with Intermediaries and Third Party Investment in Players Regulations.

"The FA charged Chelsea FC with 74 breaches of FA Rule E1.2 after its current ownership self-reported misconduct upon its purchase of the club. The FA is continuing to investigate individual misconduct arising out of this case.

"Chelsea FC admitted to the 74 breaches of FA Rule E1.2 prior to a hearing and an independent Regulatory Commission imposed a six-point deduction, which was to be suspended until 30 June 2027, and a £10 million fine."

‌



"The club appealed against the suspended points deduction, and an independent Appeal Board allowed the appeal and set aside this sanction following a further hearing. In its place, the Appeal Board imposed a registration ban for two complete and consecutive transfer windows, which is suspended until 30 June 2027.

"The £10 million fine imposed by the Regulatory Commission was not subject to appeal, and the full amount will be invested into grassroots football. The Regulatory Commission and Appeal Board's written reasons for their decisions can be found below."

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Chelsea subsequently released a statement, which read: " Chelsea Football Club is pleased to confirm that a final decision has been reached by The FA's judicial bodies in relation to historical regulatory matters that were self-reported by the club.

"In 2022, the Club self-reported potential historical rule breaches to all applicable regulators. Following that report, it has worked openly and transparently with all regulators, including voluntarily and proactively disclosing many thousands of documents.

"As previously announced, settlement agreements have been entered into with UEFA and the Premier League concerning the same self-reported regulatory matters and topics that have been addressed before. The club is pleased to confirm that, now The FA process has concluded, this brings all regulatory proceedings against the club to a close.

Article continues below

"We are grateful to UEFA, the Premier League and The FA for their engagement with the Club throughout these processes."

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Vinicius Jr update, Bruno Guimaraes latest and Man Utd step up move
Sports.content:
Chelsea and FA drop Mykhailo Mudryk statement

Mykhailo Mudryk will now be available to play for Chelsea. A statement from the FA confirmed the news, saying: "The FA can confirm that the anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against Mykhailo Mudryk were resolved with the agreement of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) on 30 July 2026.

"In the context of that agreement, Mr Mudryk has accepted his commission of Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRVs) and accepted a period of ineligibility. On 22 October 2024, Mr Mudryk was subject to an out-of-competition doping control, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance.

"The FA notified Mr Mudryk of that finding on 4 December 2024 and imposed a provisional suspension. On 23 May 2025, The FA charged Mr Mudryk with ADRVs in breach of Regulations 3 and 4 of its 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"On 7 to 9 January 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission. The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility. Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

"Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted.

"Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, The FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the Anti-Doping Rule Violations charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

Chelsea also uploaded their own statement which said: "Chelsea FC acknowledges today's announcement by The Football Association confirming the resolution of the anti-doping proceedings involving Mykhailo Mudryk.

"From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

"We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process. We welcome the acknowledgement that advances in the applicable scientific reporting standards for more reliable testing mean that, had Misha's sample been analysed under today's technical requirements, it would not have been reported as a positive test and no anti-doping rule violation would have resulted.

"That is an important part of the context surrounding the agreed resolution and allows everyone involved to move forward. "Misha has consistently maintained that he never knowingly or intentionally used a prohibited substance and did not know how traces of the substance entered his system. Throughout this process he has conducted himself professionally and with resilience during what has undoubtedly been one of the most challenging periods of his career.

"We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career. Chelsea FC remains fully committed to the highest standards of sporting integrity and compliance with all anti-doping regulations. Everyone at the Club now looks forward to helping Misha return to full fitness, back into the squad and back onto the pitch."

Sports.title: New Newcastle boss makes Bruno Guimaraes stance clear amid Arsenal offer
Sports.content:
New Newcastle boss makes Bruno Guimaraes stance clear amid Arsenal offer

Arsenal are closing in on a deal for Newcastle United star Bruno Guimaraes but it appears that new Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle is keen to keep him at St James’ Park as long as possible

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes has been linked with a move to Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Incoming Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle is set to hold face-to-face talks with Bruno Guimaraes amid interest from Arsenal. The Gunners have the Brazilian midfielder as one of their prime targets alongside compatriot Vinicius Jr.

‌



An agreement is expected to be reached between the two clubs over the coming days, with a fee expected to reach at least £80million, potentially up to £85m with add-ons.

‌



Despite Guimaraes now looking likely to become an Arsenal player before the end of the transfer window, new Newcastle head coach Jaissle is keen for talks. The 38-year-old is expected to be appointed as Eddie Howe’s replacement at St James’ Park after his exit was confirmed on Friday.

‌



According to Chronicle Live, Jaissle wants a sit-down with his new players as part of his efforts to sell his vision and philosophy. Guimaraes is among those that he wants to talk to.

Vinicius Jr moves step closer to Arsenal transfer after Real Madrid make contract decision READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes shares emotional Eddie Howe message after Newcastle exit READ MORE :

Jaissle will fly into Newcastle’s training camp at La Manga on Saturday, while the midfielder will return on Sunday having been granted an extended break after the World Cup, with the idea that he will return to work the following day.

Guimaraes’ return comes in the midst of him bidding a fond farewell to former boss Howe. Taking to social media, he wrote: "Ed, how could I ever put into words how grateful I am to you? First of all, I want to thank you for bringing me to this club. Thank you for everything you've done for me, for helping me grow not only as a player, but more importantly, as a person.

‌



"You gave me the honour of being captain - of being your captain. That is something I will never forget and will carry with me for the rest of my life.

View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle is expected to be named as Newcastle's next manager (Image: Getty Images)

"Sharing the day-to-day with you and having you as my manager has been a privilege. I'm truly grateful for every opportunity, for the trust you placed in me, and for every moment we shared together.

‌



"Without a doubt, you are one of the best managers I've ever had. Please know that my gratitude will always remain, and that you will always have a friend in me.

"Thank you for everything. I wish you and your family nothing but happiness, success, and all the very best. With affection, Bruno."

Howe in the meantime gave a final update on Guimaraes’ future in the aftermath of a pre-season defeat at the hands of Bristol City. He said: "What will be, will be.

Article continues below

“We can't control the forces that are at play here, we've just got to make sure that when Bruno comes back, we look after him and he trains well, which I'm sure he will do. And he makes a difference as he always has done.

"We've spoken numerous times. Assurances? I don't think you can push too hard for those. I've said many times we want players who are committed, and Bruno has always been committed. His training performances and his game performances have been outstanding, every time he's worn the shirt, he's played with the fans by his side. I'd love to see that continue."

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham shows true colours as England hero sent on Barcelona 'spying mission'
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham shows true colours as England hero sent on Barcelona 'spying mission'

Jude Bellingham appeared at a Barcelona pre-season game

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham watched his former club Birmingham take on Barcelona (Image: Getty Images)

Jude Bellingham changed his outfit midway through his former club Birmingham City's pre-season friendly clash with Barcelona. The Real Madrid sensation took the opportunity to observe his bitter rivals Barca ahead of the new season, where the two Spanish giants are expected to go toe-to-toe for the La Liga crown once more.

‌



Bellingham returned to his boyhood club Birmingham on Friday in his first public appearance since returning to the UK from his holiday in Hawaii. The trip came after his heroics for England at the World Cup, where his seven goals launched him into an entirely new stratosphere.

‌



The Three Lions superstar was spotted in attendance at St. Andrew’s alongside his parents Denise and Mark. His appearance in the stands didn’t go unnoticed as he was cheered and given a rousing ovation by the home crowd.

‌



FOLLOW OUR REAL MADRID FB PAGE! Latest news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jude Bellingham's parting shot to Argentina referee in unseen World Cup footage READ MORE :

Bellingham was seen celebrating both of Birmingham's goals in the entertaining 2-2 draw and he even stayed for the penalty shootout, which Chris Davies’ side won.

Upon his arrival, the 23-year-old wore a plain white top before slipping into the new Birmingham jersey at half-time. His touching gesture clearly endeared himself further to the Blues fans.

‌



Bellingham made his senior debut for Birmingham as a 16-year-old and quickly established himself as one of the brightest young talents in English football. His rapid development earned him a move to Borussia Dortmund, where he became one of Europe's top midfielders before joining Real Madrid in the summer of 2023.

View 2 Images He changed into a Birmingham shirt in a heart-warming moment at St Andrew's (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

His move helped the Blues at a time of financial difficulty, and they retired the No.22 shirt for his services to the club, despite him being a mere teenager at the time. His appearance on Friday wouldn't have only pleased Birmingham supporters, however.

‌



His new Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho would have also been delighted to see him observing rivals Barcelona, given he can now report back to the Portuguese head coach with a fresh report on the Catalans.

Barca were missing the bulk of their squad on Friday due to the World Cup, with coach Hansi Flick forced to name an inexperienced side after a week of training at St. George's Park.

The Catalans were without all eight of their Spain internationals who lifted the trophy in North America this summer. Anthony Gordon, Jules Kounde and Raphinha did not feature, either, although there was a debut for summer signing Karim Adeyemi.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino is so delusional he does not know his time is well and truly up
Sports.content:
Of the many remarkable things about the whole World Cup sell-off saga, one stands out. Power had made Gianni Infantino so delusional he thought his plot would not be destroyed by all those who care about football. Power had detached him from reality. Infantino is an intelligent man. A multi-linguist, a highly-qualified lawyer.

So how did he ever think his proposal to allow private investors to run the World Cup would even get a semblance of support from ANYONE with a remote interest in the game? How can you not read the room? How can you be so detached from reality?

Because power has made you feel untouchable. It beggars belief but it really does seem as though the proposal which has now been ditched was entirely the work of Infantino himself, aided, you assume, by his investor acquaintances who were looking to make hundreds of millions out of the World Cup.

Because anyone else in the world’s governing body could have seen what was coming. Outrage on a scale football governance has not known before.

‌



But even his chief operating officer (COO) did not know. Of all the statements denouncing Infantino and his plan, Kevin Lamour’s was the most damning.

He called it ‘the project of one person’. Lamour, FIFA COO spoke about ‘a lack of trust, a lack of transparency, a lack of discernment, a lack of good governance, and a serious lack of respect.’ He spoke of 'contempt' and 'intimidation'.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino was clearly delighted to be considered a friend of Donald Trump's (Image: Getty Images)

Lamour said ‘FIFA’s own administration was deceived’. And of the many reasons why Infantino’s position is untenable, they do not come any more emphatic than that.

‌



“Our mission,” says Lamour, “is to serve football. Not to serve the personal interests of a person who, unfortunately, believes he embodies FIFA when he is supposed to be at its service.”

And there you have it. Power has made Infantino delusional. In the late-night statement announcing the abrupt termination of his heinous scheme, there was no contrition from Infantino.

Instead, he said the scheme “was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.” If that was the case, how come he did not, by the looks of it, consult ANYONE in the FIFA organisation when hatching the plan?

View 3 Images UEFA and its president Aleksander Ceferin dealt the killer blow to Gianni Infantino's World Cup scheme (Image: Getty Images)

‌



In his statement shelving the proposals, he also talks about ‘moving forward’, but quite clearly, FIFA cannot move forward when its president has lost the confidence of the overwhelming majority of stakeholders in the game. And when we say ‘overwhelming majority’, we could probably say ‘all’.

The next president will be elected in March at a congress in Morocco. As it stands, Infantino will be unopposed.

That cannot happen. Other candidates need to come forward ahead of a nomination deadline in November. But the election should happen sooner because Infantino should resign.

All those nations who got together to oppose Infantino’s FIFA Forward Enterprise project should now declare their complete lack of confidence in the organisation’s leader. His time is well and truly up. But the power has made him so delusional, he probably does not know it.

‌

Sports.title: UEFA declare loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino in bombshell new statement
Sports.content:
UEFA declare loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino in bombshell new statement

Gianni Infantino has scrapped his controversial plan to sell off a share of the World Cup to private investors but his move has left European football furious

View 2 Images UEFA have hit back at Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

UEFA have declared a loss of confidence in beleaguered FIFA president Gianni Infantino after his World Cup sale scandal.

‌



Infantino confirmed the plot to sell-off a share in the tournament to private investors this week, only to perform a dramatic u-turn after considerable backlash.

‌



UEFA threatened a wide-ranging boycott of any FIFA tournaments, while fellow federations such as CONCACAF and AFC also publicised their opposition to the plan. O ne of Infantino’s closest advisors, Carlos Cordeiro, resigned from his post, while FIFA Chief Operating Officer Kevin Lamour slammed the plan.

‌



Things have now grown even worse for the FIFA president, with European football's governing body remaining furious and demanding he be removed from office.

A statement from UEFA read: "We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

‌



"It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA's Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA. You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA,' before telling the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of FIFA is your money. It's not the money of the FIFA President. It's your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.'

"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through were anything but transparent."

‌



Infantino, 56, has been president of FIFA since February 2016, having replaced Sepp Blatter. He previously worked at UEFA, having been at the corporation since 2000. He claimed the role as Secretary General in 2009 before receiving the backing of the UEFA Executive Committee to stand for the position of FIFA President in 2015.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been forced to perform an embarrassing u-turn (Image: Getty Images)

UEFA's bombshell statement comes less than 12 hours after FIFA confirmed that they had completed a u-turn and scrapped their plan.

‌



A statement in the early hours of Saturday morning read: “The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

“And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

“Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.

‌



“Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

“Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.”

Sports.title: Richarlison scores late winner as 10-man Spurs beat Chelsea
Sports.content:
Richarlison scored a 92nd-minute winner for Tottenham as they beat Chelsea 2-1 in Sydney despite Kevin Danso being sent off in the second half.

The Spurs substitute pounced on a loose ball in the box after Jamie Donley's shot had ricocheted off the post, tapping it into an empty net with virtually the last kick of the game to make it four wins from four in pre-season for Roberto De Zerbi's side.

Sandro Tonali opened the scoring in the 21st minute with his first goal for Tottenham since making his £100m switch from Newcastle, but that was quickly cancelled out by Estevao's header.

Danso's red card, four minutes after coming on at the break, looked to put the game into Chelsea's control but Xabi Alonso's team failed to make the advantage count.

They had just four shots on target, the same amount as Spurs, despite the red card for their opponents. Antonin Kinsky thwarted any chance Chelsea did have, denying Joao Pedro and Estevao with two fine saves.

The winner came from a rare counter-attack by the new-look Spurs side, who defended well throughout with Andy Robertson making his first start and Jan Paul van Hecke on debut, as they battled to secure another win in pre-season.

Sports.title: Root: I won't rip up Bazball blueprint
Sports.content:
England captain Joe Root says he does not want to "completely rip everything up" from the Bazball era after becoming Test captain for the second time in his career.

The 35-year-old Yorkshireman has been reappointed as Test skipper following the retirement of Ben Stokes and the arrival of new coach Stephen Fleming.

Root led England between 2017 and 2022, captaining them a record 65 times. He left his position after managing just one victory in his final 17 matches, as well as a 4-0 defeat in The Ashes.

England's style became much more attacking under McCullum and Stokes, but it had taken somewhat of a sour turn before the former was sacked and Stokes left. However, Root says he will not run away from 'Bazball'.

Speaking to the ECB, Root said: "Since 2022 we've done some amazing things.

"We'll try to continue a lot of the good stuff we did over that period and not finding ourselves back to where we were before Baz [Brendon McCullum] and Ben [Stokes] took over, and evolving and tweaking things to where we want to be and really competing against the top nations consistently."

Root's appointment raised some eyebrows given the nature of his previous departure from the captaincy, as well as fans sighting worries over the role affecting his batting.

His average as skipper during his last stint was almost seven runs below an average of 53.34 without the 'armband'.

However, Root believes a lot has changed since he stepped down - including himself.

Image: Root is back as England Test captain following the retirement of Ben Stokes

"[I'm] hugely different, anyone that says in an eight-year period they were the same person they were [at the start] is probably lying," he said.

"Whether it be within the game, away from it, all the experience you have along the way throughout that period you will be shaped into a slightly different person. I think that will be very similar in how I want to take this team forward."

Fleming, former captain of the New Zealand national team, recently left his role as head coach of Indian Premier League franchise Chennai Super Kings to join England's Test team.

Asked about working with Fleming, Root said: "We've spoken briefly and if I'm being brutally honest he was a big reason why I wanted to do it.

"I'm very excited by the way he sees the game, where he sees us sit as a team and the work we have to do to get to where we want to get to.

Image: Stephen Fleming will be working with Root to reignite English Test cricket

"All of that got me very excited about taking this role on. Very much looking forward to working with him and he's obviously got a wealth of experience, done some amazing things in the game as a player and as a coach.

"I'm looking forward to the next little while and us trying to build something pretty special together."

Root takes charge for the upcoming three-match series against Pakistan this month.
