Sports.title: One month to go....what your PL club still needs to do in summer window
Sports.content:
Arsenal

Arsenal have the bulk of their business still to do after bringing in Christos Tzolis for £34m as a Leandro Trossard replacement and Illan Meslier as a third-choice goalkeeper on a free transfer after his departure from Leeds.

The Premier League champions have ambitious plans to capitalise on their title success by targeting elite signings for the left-wing and central-midfield positions. Work has been done to explore the cost of potential deals for Brazil stars Vinicius Junior and Bruno Guimaraes.

Vinicius, who has entered the final year of his deal at Real Madrid, is one of the options Arsenal are considering along with PSG's Bradley Barcola and Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez after refusing to meet Aston Villa's valuation of top target Morgan Rogers.

However, Sky Sports News has been told Real Madrid are confident Vinicius will sign a new contract and he is not expected to leave this summer. The Brazilian is entering the final year of his deal, and Arsenal continue to monitor his situation.

Arsenal want to sign Guimaraes to bolster the midfield, and he has told Newcastle he would like to join the Gunners. Discussions have taken place through intermediaries about the figures it would take to do a deal, but Newcastle do not want to sell.

Arsenal also have big plans to raise funds from outgoings, an area in which they have historically struggled, with uncertainty around the futures of Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus, who is valued at £18m-£20m, as they enter the final year of their contracts.

Martinelli's deal includes a club-held option for a further year, protecting Arsenal from losing him for nothing in a year should the right conditions for a sale not materialise this summer. It is unlikely that his sale would be sanctioned without the arrival of another left-winger.

Ben White has attracted interest from the likes of Everton, but injuries to Jurrien Timber and William Saliba could impact Arsenal's willingness to let the England defender go. It remains to be seen if Timber is going to be fit for the start of the season.

Arsenal are exploring options at centre-back in light of the news that Saliba's back injury would keep him out for an extended period. John Stones was under consideration but has joined Inter, while there is a gap in valuation with Aston Villa for Ezri Konsa.

Aston Villa

Sky Sports News reported Aston Villa would likely have to sell a major name or two to stay in line with UEFA's financial rules, and Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers have departed for a combined fee of £152m.

Johan Manzambi, Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho have arrived to bolster Unai Emery's squad ahead of their return to the Champions League - but more numbers are needed with the futures of Leon Bailey and Emiliano Martinez also uncertain.

Hull City are close to signing Bailey, who has one year left on his deal, while links to Juventus for Martinez refuse to go away. Juve are exploring alternatives due to the gap in valuation, one of which is Zion Suzuki, who is on Villa's keeper shortlist in case Martinez goes.

Villa are one of several clubs in the Premier League and Europe to express interest in Chelsea striker Nicolas Jackson but will be unable to loan him from Chelsea, having already signed Garnacho on a temporary deal, and a permanent move is complicated by UEFA's rules.

There is also interest in a temporary move for midfielder Joao Palhinha, but Bayern Munich want a permanent deal for the 31-year-old, who spent last season at Tottenham. Benfica and Palhinha's former club Sporting have also been interested in a summer move.

Ollie Watkins' future is also one to watch. Sky Sports News reported Fenerbahce were one of the clubs interested in signing the 30-year-old forward, who has two years remaining on his deal at Villa.

Bournemouth

Bournemouth hope to complete the signing of central defender Antonio Silva from Benfica this weekend, filling a priority position following the exit of Marcos Senesi, but beyond that there is no rush to make wholesale changes after big spending in recent windows.

Work is being done to explore the options to replace Alex Jimenez at right-back following his move to Fiorentina on an initial loan, with Adam Smith currently the only option available to new head coach Marco Rose ahead of Bournemouth's debut European campaign.

Bournemouth are considering the potential of bringing in a No 6 and a No 10, while adding a winger is another possibility if the right opportunity presented itself. But there is no longer a desire to bring in a goalkeeper as Rose is happy with his options behind Djordje Petrovic.

As far as Bournemouth are concerned, they are not anticipating any big departures, and they are under no pressure to let any of them go. Alex Scott has plenty of Premier League interest, while Eli Junior Kroupi's foot injury all but ends the slim chances of a summer exit.

Brentford

Brentford's priority this summer has been to sign a new central midfielder to build their future team under Keith Andrews.

It has been something they have been working on since January, when they looked at PSV's Joey Veerman among others, and it has been made even more pressing recently by the departure of Jordan Henderson.

Brentford allowed him to speak to their west London neighbours Chelsea about a free transfer, and so - in the midst of that - they are set to bring in highly-rated Lens midfielder Mamadou Sangare for up to £41m.

He is more of a defensive midfield anchor who could recycle and build from deep. Later in the window, the Bees may be open to another more advanced midfield addition, while left-back is also an area of consideration.

Brentford will fight to keep the likes of Kevin Schade, who is of interest to Roma although a deal looks beyond them financially. The Bees would look to bring in a top left winger in the event a club made them an offer they could not refuse for Schade.

Ethan Pinnock could move on given Brentford have already signed a new centre-back in Jannik Schuster, while Gustavo Nunes, Jayden Meghoma and Yunus Emre Konak may need to go out on loan for more game-time to aid their development.

Brighton

Brighton are in the market for reinforcements up front, in midfield and on the wing. There is a desire to bring in cover for Kaoru Mitoma on the left as he is out for the start of the season, while Chelsea-bound Danny Welbeck needs replacing.

Their plans to target a new midfielder are not a sign that long-term Manchester United target Carlos Baleba is off anywhere. Brighton want to keep him and add more depth in the middle of the park for Fabian Hurzeler ahead of their European campaign in the new season.

As things stand, however, the priorities are improving the forward line with a new wide attacker and a No 9. Brighton have relied on Welbeck's goals in the last two Premier League seasons and finding a player with the capacity to fill his boots will not be easy.

Both their current striking options, Stefanos Tzimas and Charalampos Kostoulas, are highly rated but yet to prove themselves in the Premier League. Brighton were one of many Premier League sides credited with an interest in Carlos Espi before he joined Real Madrid.

Carl Rushworth is set to follow Welbeck out of the exit door as he makes his move to Coventry permanent, while defender Igor Julio does not feature in Hurzeler's plans and has interest from Espanyol and other clubs in Europe.

Ibrahim Osman and Facundo Buonanotte could join Tommy Watson in going out on loan. The former Sunderland winger is close to joining Leicester. Eiran Cashin is also expected to depart.

Chelsea

Chelsea have been the biggest spenders in the Premier League so far, but they are not done yet, with central midfield another area they could recruit in despite the expected arrival of Jordan Henderson on a free transfer following his exit from Brentford.

There is a strong interest in Alex Scott, but Bournemouth are sticking to their guns over the midfielder. The future of Enzo Fernandez, who has flirted with a Chelsea exit for some time now, could be decisive if they are to bring in a midfielder for big money.

Danny Welbeck, another Premier League veteran, is following Henderson through the door at Stamford Bridge as Xabi Alonso adds much-needed experience to his squad following a change in transfer policy at Chelsea that pre-dates his appointment.

Welbeck's arrival leaves Chelsea with a surplus of strikers. Sales are nearly just as important as signing for Chelsea given their UEFA settlement and bloated squad. Nicolas Jackson and Liam Delap are among the players that could leave Stamford Bridge this summer.

Alonso has just brought in Maxence Lacroix at centre-back to take Chelsea up to 10 players in that position, and he wants to cut that number down to around five. Trevoh Chalobah, Axel Disasi and Benoit Badiashile are among the players in that position who could go.

Chelsea have been in talks to sign left-back Pep Chavarria for a few weeks without being able to bridge the gap in valuation with Rayo Vallecano. The 28-year-old would help fill the gap left by Marc Cucurella, although Jorell Hato is also expected to play more at left-back.

Coventry

The newly-promoted side have made two new additions to their squad from last season by signing central defender Aurele Amenda from Eintracht Frankfurt for around £17.2m and winger Loum Tchaouna from Burnley in a £20m deal.

Frank Lampard still wants to strengthen his side further and is close to doing so with the acquisition of goalkeeper Carl Rushworth from Brighton for an initial fee of £22.5m plus add-ons. He made a big impression on loan in their promotion season.

Once that deal is completed, Coventry want to bring in a left-back and a right winger, while there is also a possibility they target a new striker. They are also in talks to bring Gustavo Hamer back from Sheffield United as he enters the final year of his deal.

Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace's new boss Pierre Sage has only been able to bring in one new signing so far this summer. Free agent defender Oscar Mingueza can play as a right-back and a central defender and provides Palace with the flexibility they need for five at the back.

Palace are yet to properly replace Marc Guehi and now need to find a successor to Maxence Lacroix, with centre-back a top priority. Palace have ended talks with Augsburg for Chrislain Matsima and have a number of alternative options.

Among those have been Toulouse's Charlie Cresswell, Lyon's Ruben Kluivert and Trabzonspor's Chibuike Nwaiwu, who is also of interest to Fulham.

Retaining Daichi Kamada in midfield will not go down as a new signing but was a crucial piece of business for Palace. They still have designs on bringing in further additions in midfield but Kamada's renewal for another year has eased the urgency on that front.

Palace admire Southampton's Shea Charles, who is a target for Leeds, as a potential option to strengthen the midfield. As of yet, there has been no club-to-club contact with Southampton.

There is interest in adding another forward player who can play in one of those wide No 10 roles behind the striker in the 3-4-2-1 formation that Sage is expected to continue with at Selhurst Park.

Jean-Philippe Mateta has entered the final year of his deal and nearly joined AC Milan in January. Palace may cash in on him if the right offer arrives and would need to sign a replacement in that scenario.

Adam Wharton has interest from a number of top clubs in the Premier League, but Palace will not want to let him go. The England international has three years to run on his deal and would not come cheap.

Everton

David Moyes still has plenty of business to do at Everton in the final month of the window and chief among his priorities is bringing in a right-back. It has been confirmed by Martin O'Neill that Everton have approached Celtic for Canada international Alistair Johnston.

Elsewhere, bringing in a replacement for Idrissa Gana Gueye is another key area of focus. Everton have added Hayden Hackney from Middlesbrough, but his big strength is on the ball, and Gueye's exit leaves Moyes short of a destroyer in the middle of the park.

Everton also want to sign a striker as they search for a more consistent source of goals with neither Thierno Barry nor Beto delivering on that front so far. Liam Delap was a target before he joined Chelsea last summer and Everton have looked into a potential deal again.

Tyrique George's loan has been made permanent after Everton negotiated a new fee with Chelsea, but it remains to be seen if Jack Grealish will be able to return following his season on Merseyside. Everton were unwilling to pay the £50m option to buy in his loan.

Everton are still keen to add another winger after George, and there is interest in Newcastle's Jacob Murphy, who was a favourite of the now departed Eddie Howe at St James' Park and has entered the final year of his contract. Interest in Grealish also remains.

Those plans could change if Iliman Ndiaye were to move on. Everton are aware of interest from Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal, but there has been no formal approach or contact with them, and they have no appetite to sell the 26-year-old, who has three years on his deal.

Fulham

Fulham are starting to do some business now that Alvaro Arbeloa's feet are under the table as new head coach.

They have agreed a combined £42.3m deal for a pair of Real Madrid youth graduates that played under Arbeloa there last season; striker Gonzalo Garcia and midfielder Cesar Palacios.

Arbeloa was the driving force behind these moves, and Garcia certainly answers the issue of who their new centre-forward would be, following the departure of Raul Jimenez. Garcia and Rodrigo Muniz are two good options.

Fulham still need a number of other positions strengthening, however, including wingers following the departure of Harry Wilson on a free transfer to Leeds United and Samuel Chukwueze returning to AC Milan following a loan spell.

There also appears to be more work to do in midfield, especially amid uncertainty around the future of Sander Berge, who has interest from Manchester United and several other clubs. Another battling midfielder may come into the club.

Fulham are also interested in signing a central defender to replace Issa Diop after his move to Ipswich. Trabzonspor's Chibuike Nwaiwu is one of the defenders on the club's list of options.

Hull

Acun Ilicali, the Hull owner, has not been shy to provide updates about their transfer business this summer, and so he could be very busy on social media for the rest of the window with 12 signings expected to arrive before the window shuts.

The promoted side have plans to strengthen in every position, with midfield the priority. By signing free agent Hidemasa Morita, they have answered the need for a holding player, while talks are ongoing to sign Florentino from Burnley, and he will add more legs in midfield.

Hull's owner has said the deal to sign winger Leon Bailey from Aston Villa in a permanent transfer is close to being done, while they are also pursuing defender Nobel Mendy from Rayo Vallecano and midfielder Mert Komur from Augsburg.

Ilicali's post on X, which revealed the nationalities of the players Hull were pursuing and gave us a progress report, shows there are a lot more irons in the fire as the promoted side work to ensure Sergej Jakirovic has a strong enough squad to avoid relegation.

Ipswich

The promoted side have been busy in this transfer window so far, spending around £80m on six new arrivals, but Ipswich still have plans to bring in more players over the next month.

New boss Gary O'Neil has been dealing with a few injury issues in midfield, and that is an area he hopes to recruit in before the end of the window. Bringing in players with experience, preferably of the Premier League, is key for Ipswich.

That is why Fulham's Sasa Lukic is among a number of midfielders they are considering this summer. The Serbia international has one year left on his deal, which means this is potentially Fulham's last opportunity to make some money back off him through a sale.

Elsewhere, Sky Sports News revealed that Ipswich are interested in re-signing Julio Enciso, who spent a spell on loan at Portman Road in 2025. The former Brighton player is currently playing for Chelsea's partner club Strasbourg in France, where he played under O'Neil.

Jaden Philogene wants to leave Ipswich this summer, Sky Sports News understands, amid interest from a number of clubs in Europe. Ipswich would be open to permanent offers for the winger, who has three years to run on his contract.

New goalkeeper signing Kayne van Oevelen could go out on loan, while striker George Hirst and right-back Harry Clarke both have Championship interest but Ipswich are seeking permanent offers.

Leeds

Leeds are considering alternative options after missing out on Julian Brandt to Ajax. This has been the case since they set off for their pre-season tour of the US, wary of the time it had taken for the 30-year-old to make a decision on his future.

The plan this summer has always been to bring in players who improve the individual quality in the squad with a capacity to make the difference in the final third.

It remains to be seen if Leeds will target a No 10 or a winger capable of playing inside now that Brandt is off the table. Noah Okafor is the only player in this mould of the current options capable of playing on the left.

Leeds are closing in on a club-record deal for Manchester City goalkeeper James Trafford, which is worth an initial £40m plus add-ons. The England international's arrival is expected to pave the way for Lucas Perri to join Torino on an initial loan.

There will need to be another goalkeeper signing to provide cover for Trafford after Karl Darlow chose to join Manchester United over extending his deal with Leeds. As things stand, Alex Cairns, who has not played a senior game since 2024, is the only other option.

Central midfield remains a position Leeds are keen to add in despite so far failing to reach an agreement with Southampton for Shea Charles. Leeds will not improve on their third offer but have left it on the table in case Saints reconsider their position.

Leeds are also looking to bring in another striker to provide cover for Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha, who both have patchy injury records. Finding a versatile defender, in the mould of James Justin, who can play both left and right-back, is also on Leeds' list.

In terms of outgoings, Perri seems closest to an exit, but that will likely have to wait until Trafford's mandated holiday after the World Cup is over or a No 2 arrives. Joel Piroe and Wilfried Gnonto are among the other players who are likely to move on as well this summer.

Leeds made a strong start to the window by signing long-term target Harry Wilson on a free transfer to improve their wide attacking options as well as moving swiftly to bring in Tarik Muharemovic for £34m from Sassuolo as a replacement for Pascal Struijk.

Liverpool

Bringing in a wide attacker is the priority for Liverpool heading into the final month of the window. They plan to open talks with PSG forward Bradley Barcola, but it will be a difficult deal to do with the French and European champions valuing him at around £145m.

Barcola has been unhappy in Paris due to his role, particularly in the biggest games, and PSG are open to letting him go if his feelings do not change, as long as they receive what they deem to be an acceptable offer for a top player with two years left on his deal.

It remains to be seen which player Liverpool plan to start on the right wing following Mohamed Salah's exit if they sign Barcola. The France star prefers playing on the left, which is the favoured side of rising star Rio Ngumoha and Cody Gakpo.

Jeremie Frimpong, who has so far failed to convince at right-back, is expected to be used in a more advanced role while new signing Victor Munoz is also capable of being deployed on the right-hand side.

Joe Gomez's injury, which will force him to miss the start of the Premier League season, has not changed Liverpool's transfer plans. Signing a central defender is not seen as a priority despite Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni coming off the back of long-term lay-offs.

As things stand, Liverpool are expected to only have two senior central defenders available when they kick off the season against Newcastle on August 23: Virgil van Dijk, only just returning from his post-World Cup break, and Jacquet, who has not played since February.

Liverpool's stance could change as the window progresses. An option, like Gomez, who can play both right-back and centre-back, would solve a lot of problems. A left-back could also be signed if Kostas Tsimikas fails to convince Andoni Iraola, but every player has a clean slate.

Ryan Gravenberch's emergence as a No 6 in Arne Slot's first year put plans to bring in a holding midfielder further down the priority list at Liverpool, but the team's performances in the season just gone have highlighted a need for reinforcements in that position.

Inter want to sign Curtis Jones, but as things stand their valuation falls well short of Liverpool's, especially in a market when other Premier League proven players in his position have moved for such big fees. Harvey Elliott, like Jones, faces an uncertain future.

Man City

Manchester City's window is in danger of becoming bittersweet. The £116m signing of Elliot Anderson is seen as a huge coup considering every other club in Europe wanted to sign him. However, the chances of Rodri departing for Real Madrid seem to be increasing.

Sky Sports News reported at the end of the week that Real Madrid are expected to make an offer for Spain's World Cup-winning captain, having made initial contact. City are determined to keep him and give him a new long-term deal, but it may come down to the wishes of Rodri himself, who is recovering after back surgery.

City are contingency planning like any club would and are believed to be in talks with Lille to sign the highly rated 18-year-old Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, who impressed at the World Cup.

City also want to continue improving their attack, with a top left-winger still in the offing too. They were one of the clubs in for Yan Diomande, but he also looks destined for Real Madrid. Pedro Neto has been linked with a move to City and a potential reunion with Enzo Maresca.

City are also keen on a young striker to develop behind Erling Haaland and offer a different option and are one of the clubs keen on Eli Junior Kroupi, who Bournemouth say is not for sale. However, his injury makes a move even more unlikely.

A young right-back is another position City are interested in adding in, while, in terms of outgoings, goalkeeper James Trafford is close to joining Leeds so will need to be replaced.

Man Utd

Manchester United continue to see what market opportunities may arise for them to further strengthen Michael Carrick's side in the last month of the window.

United are considering possible additions at left-back and midfield. They have begun exploring what a potential move could look like for Newcastle United's Lewis Hall. They have been long-term admirers of the 21-year-old, who has three years left on his deal.

Roma's Manu Kone, Brighton's Carlos Baleba and Bournemouth's Tyler Adams are among a number of midfield options being considered.

There have also been suggestions that the club are not guaranteed to further reinforce the midfield after the signings of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, but much will depend on outgoings and what opportunities may arise in the coming weeks.

Mason Mount has played in a deeper midfield role at the end of last season as well as pre-season; however, his injury record remains a concern. Academy product Tyler Fletcher is pushing to be involved in the first team this season as another option.

Newcastle

Image: Matthias Jaissle is set replace Eddie Howe as Newcastle head coach

This has already been a seismic transfer window for Newcastle and the final month has the potential to bring even more change, with uncertainty over the future of Bruno Guimaraes amid strong interest from Arsenal and Manchester United exploring a move for Lewis Hall.

Newcastle have already committed to spending more than £140m this summer on five players, if you include the proposed deal for their soon-to-be new first-choice goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, as they use the funds from Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon's sales.

They have already signed a left winger in Bazoumana Toure and two midfielders in Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba, while Ewen Jaouen has arrived as a deputy goalkeeper. Newcastle are also looking to bring in a versatile full-back who can play on the left and right.

Further arrivals are likely to be dependent on outgoings - and not just those high-profile names mentioned earlier - with Jacob Murphy and Joe Willock attracting interest in this window. Nick Pope could also go, with his replacements basically through the door already.

Newcastle have changed policy to focus on signing younger players with high potential in the range of £20m-£40m this summer, but it remains to be seen how that might change if Guimaraes or Hall, neither of whom they are inviting offers for, were to leave.

Nottingham Forest

Forest's immediate need is obvious - how do they fill the Elliot Anderson-shaped hole in their midfield?

Lucas Bergvall is the man they want, but getting Spurs to sell for a price they are happy with is proving difficult.

Oliver Glasner is spending Forest's pre-season camp in the Algarve as a way to weigh-up his squad and figure out the system he thinks suits them best. If he opts for three at the back, then another centre-back will be brought in, perhaps two if Morato is sold.

Talks continue with Sporting for Ousmane Diomande, who has been a long-term target for Glasner dating back to his time as Crystal Palace boss. The Austrian is believed to be driving Forest's pursuit of the Ivory Coast international.

Do not rule out a move for a centre-forward too. Glasner told us recently how much Forest missed Chris Wood last season, but a younger No 9 may be targeted.

Sunderland

Last summer's most active club are not planning to be so busy this time around. Bringing in a winger and a left-back are viewed as the priorities for Regis Le Bris as they prepare the squad for their European campaign.

Sunderland are yet to make a signing in this window, but there is understood to be no panic at the Stadium of Light. This window was viewed as being an opportunity to top up the fine work of their impressive first window back as a Premier League club.

There is a long way to go in the transfer market, and so far the positions Sunderland have been looking to add in have been slow moving. Sunderland have no plans to rush into deals that are not right for them as they look to add more quality to the squad.

They are expecting to make a number of signings, potentially between four and five, which is less than half their total number of arrivals last summer. Whoever they sign, Sunderland's most important act of the window will be keeping captain Granit Xhaka.

Tottenham

Tottenham have surprised European football with their bullish attitude towards the market, smashing their wage ceiling and transfer record to buy two top midfielders in Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, and centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi said this week that they are not done in the market yet and that a "bomba" is coming, with the club turning their attentions now to improving in attack.

Manchester City's Savinho remains a top target for the left-wing position, and he wants to leave the Etihad to join Spurs. All that is left is for Tottenham to put in their first bid, which has yet to come. He is one of a number of left-wing players they have looked at, including Liverpool's Cody Gakpo.

There is every reason to believe they will not just stop at just one new forward either. Bournemouth striker Junior Kroupi is another player of interest; however, his injury may have put even further difficulty in the way of any deal being concluded. Bournemouth are determined not to sell him after just one season, and he also has Barcelona and Manchester City on his trail.

Among the other players who have interest from elsewhere and may yet find themselves being the subject of bids from other clubs are Djed Spence, Lucas Bergvall, Pape Mata Sarr, Manor Solomon - and the biggest name of all, Cristian Romero.

Atletico Madrid remain interested in the Argentina World Cup winner, who has also been a prime target for Inter Milan, who have just signed John Stones.

Despite Spurs' evaluation of Romero being higher than where the Italian champions would like it to be, they may not have given up totally on the former Atalanta player.

Sports.title: Haaderr and Suspicious Mindz clash at Doncaster
Sports.content:
We have a busy day's racing on Saturday with flat action from Doncaster and Lingfield Park live on Sky Sports Racing...

4.15 Doncaster - Haaderr and Suspicious Mindz top strong field

A strong edition of the Winners Wear Skopes Menswear Handicap sees Haaderr and Suspicious Mindz spearhead a field of five.

The Ed Bethell-trained Haaderr built on a pair of promising efforts to break his maiden at Southwell in October and, having undergone a gelding operation, he returned to a disappointing fourth of four at Catterick. That was his handicap introduction, and he could be capable of better.

Suspicious Mindz scored at the eighth attempt when landing a Curragh maiden on his final start for Jessica Harrington and he looks an interesting contender on his handicap bow for Seb Spencer.

Plenty have chances including First Time, while Vidmiyr has Jude Fernandes claiming a handy 7lbs.

5.05 Lingfield - Bintknight, Epictetus and Percival headline

Bintknight and Percival headline a field of five for this Professional Horse Racing Tips At chracingclub.com Handicap at Lingfield.

Harry Charlton's Bintknight is one of two three-year-olds in here and showed a good attitude when winning over this track and trip back in May. He made a pleasing handicap debut when runner-up at Doncaster and could go well off this one-pound higher mark.

Fellow three-year-old Starlight Time has been a tad disappointing in better company and should appreciate these calmer waters.

Percival and Epictetus must be considered. The former was a bit keen when third at Sandown and might have more to offer after just six starts, while Epictetus went down by just a neck at Epsom on his last outing.

10.52 Colonial Downs - Grade One Arlington Million Stakes - Burnham Square and Test Score clash

A brilliant field has assembled for this Grade One Arlington Million Stakes at Colonial Downs with Burnham Square sure to be popular for Ian Wilkes.

Winner of his last three outings, he justified short odds when landing the Chorleywood Stakes at Churchill Downs and will need to be at his best if he is to claim a second top-level success.

Test Score rates a big danger for Graham Motion. A dual Grade One victor, he returned to form with an excellent second in the Manhattan Stakes and a similar effort would see him hit the frame.

Of the others, Integration, Dresden Row and Gran Oriente make most appeal.

Best of the rest

4.00 Clairefontaine - Simon and Ed Crisford saddle Treble Tee in a Listed heat. Phineas is a useful type for the Wertheimers.

4.35 Clairefontaine - Listed contest where Alla Stella represents Sir Mark Prescott.

2.30am Del Mar - Grade One Clement L Hirsch Stakes - Chasten and Seismic Beauty will be popular.

10.44 Saratoga - Grade Two Jim Dandy - Renegade and Commandment headline a hot contest.

6.15 Lingfield - Tom Collins' Horse-To-Follow Campeona bids for a hat-trick.

2.30 Doncaster - A fair nursery with Encounter and Weleyff among five runners.

George Scott - 50% at Doncaster this season.

Sports.title: Leeds thrash Toulouse as Wigan beat Leigh
Sports.content:
Jake Connor starred as Super League leaders Leeds ran in eight tries in a 46-0 rout of Toulouse while Wigan Warriors remain just two points behind after their 20-8 win over Leigh Leopards.

Connor scored two of those tries himself and converted seven as the Rhinos ran up the score. Ned McCormack had an early try disallowed for a knock-on but it was merely a temporary stay of execution for Toulouse on a long night for the visitors.

Twelve minutes in Connor found a gap with the help of Riley Lumb to get the first, and it was then Connor who set up Mikolaj Oledzki for the second try of the night with a no-look pass. On the stroke of half-time Tom Holroyd added a third thanks to an offload from Presley Cassell.

The onslaught continued in the second half. James McDonnell found a gap four minutes after the restart, and just before the hour Leeds shifted the ball from wing to wing for Harry Newman to cross in the corner - although for the first time on the night Connor missed the conversion.

He made amends four minutes later by scoring his second try of the night, hauling in a catch before touching down. And Leeds kept on the pressure with late tries from Brodie Croft and Lumb padding an already lop-sided score-line.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Leeds Rhinos against Toulouse Olympique from the Super League

Wigan keep in touch with key victory

Wigan made it 10 consecutive wins in all competitions as they beat neighbours Leigh Leopards 20-8.

It was a typically full-throttle encounter from the start, with the first points scored from the boot of Leigh's Adam Cook after nine minutes following an infringement in front of the posts on Umyla Hanley.

The lead was extended to 6-0 five minutes later when the Leopards ended a period of pressure by working the ball out to Innes Senior on the left and he went over in the corner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Innes Senior dives into the corner which gave Leigh Leopards an early lead over Wigan Warriors

The Leopards threw bodies on the line to keep out Wigan as they tried to take advantage of a couple of errors from the hosts, and the visitors thought they had reduced the deficit with 29 minutes gone.

Jake Wardle broke from his own line and found Liam Marshall, who sprinted almost the length of the field to touch down in the corner, but Wardle was penalised for a push on Hanley following a video review. Cook chose to go for goal from the penalty and extended the lead to eight points.

Leigh's defence had been exceptional but three minutes before the break they switched off as Field sprinted away following a penalty deep in his own half, breaking clean through the Leopards line and reaching the posts before anyone could catch him.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matt Peet reacts to his side's victory over Leigh Leopard which extends Wigan Warriors unbeaten to eight games in the league

Harry Smith's kick reduced the arrears further, and four minutes after the break the visitors took the lead. Jack Hughes tried an extra pass, Noah Hodkinson picked up the loose ball and found Bevan French, who ran in under the posts.

Leigh coach Adrian Lam's expression darkened further in the 51st minute when his side were again made to pay dearly for a handling mistake, this time in-form Zach Eckersley intercepting and running away to the line.

And it was soon to get even worse, with smart handling from the Warriors after another Leopards error seeing Eckersley brilliantly play in Hodkinson for a fourth try in the corner.

Leigh tried to find a way back into the contest but Wigan stood firm to open up a six-point lead over their rivals and hand the Leopards a first defeat in six.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Hull KR against Bradford Bulls from the Super League

The other match on Friday saw Joe Burgess reach a career milestone of 200 tries after he scored twice in Hull KR's 40-16 win against Bradford Bulls.

Hull KR led 16-10 at half time before Jez Litten, Tom Davies and Elliot Minchella all scored in the second half to send the reigning champions into the top four.

Sports.title: Papers: Real Madrid open to Arsenal target Vinicius Jr leaving club
Sports.content:
The top stories and transfer rumours from Saturday's newspapers...

Arsenal

Real Madrid are open to the possibility of Arsenal target Vinicius Junior leaving the club if there's no agreement on a new contract for the player, with Madrid having no plans to increase their last renewal offer - ESPN

Real Madrid have tabled a final take it or leave it contract offer to Arsenal target Vinicius Junior - Marca

Arsenal have reached an agreement in principle to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle in a £77m plus add-ons, and have set aside a day next week for the Brazil midfielder's medical - Daily Mail

Sports.title: American Affair flies the flag for Goldie at Goodwood
Sports.content:
Scottish speedball American Affair bounced back to form to claim top honours in the King George Qatar Stakes at Goodwood.

Jim Goldie's stable star won the King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot last summer, but missed the remainder of the 2025 season through injury.

A second-place finish behind the reopposing Night Raider in Haydock's Temple Stakes in May suggested he retained a good level of his ability, but having trailed home last of all when defending his Ascot title and since come up short in a Listed race at York, he was a 12-1 shot for his latest Group Two assignment.

Always up with the pace in the group that raced closest to the stands rail, American Affair finished off strongly in the hands of his regular partner Paul Mulrennan to get up and beat Rumstar and Time For Sandals down the middle of the track, with Australian raider Asfoora running her best race for a while in fourth.

Goldie senior stayed closer to home, but his son, George, said: "My dad is at Musselburgh, we couldn't both come here, but I think he'll be sorry to have missed out!

"My daughter rides him every day, he's a lovely-natured horse and he's obviously very talented.

"We had faith he'd be back to this level, we've been happy with him at home but things were interrupted by the injury he had at the back end of last year.

"This year it has been a case of building him back up to his best, he showed a glimmer at Haydock three runs ago, but Ascot was a bit of a disaster - he just pulled too hard.

"He ran well at York when he was drawn badly, so we were coming here very hopeful. He's been getting back into that flow of racing properly and finishing his race off.

"We were hoping today was going to suit him better, we were coming here very hopeful."

On future plans, he added: "The plan is to go for the Nunthorpe now, then maybe the Curragh or he could go up to six (furlongs) for the Haydock Sprint Cup.

"We've not entered him in the Abbaye, the Flying Five at the Curragh after the Nunthorpe is more likely."

Weighing-room stalwart Mulrennan said: "He's done everything right today so, touch wood, he comes back from this good. We'll enjoy today, but we've got the Nunthorpe and possibly America would be nice.

"At this stage of the game I've probably got more years behind me than in front of me, but I feel I'm still going strong. It's very competitive, it's hard. I've only got one ride down here this week, but we've made it count.

"I've got my driver with me, Adele (wife). The last time I won it was on Moviesta, Adele drove me then. I've won this race twice and I probably should have won it twice again - Easton Angel probably should have won and Moviesta another year was unlucky, so it's been an unlucky race for me and a lucky race for me, but we got it right today."

Wendy McGrandles of Barraston Racing, who own American Affair with Goldie, said: "He's had one or two excuses and we always felt that he was as good as he was last year. It's once in a lifetime for us, small breeders.

"I remember him as a foal and thinking we could maybe send him eventing if he wasn't fast enough to go racing. He was broken in to go eventing because we weren't sure whether he would be big enough or fast enough to be a racehorse. He can always do that as a second career!"

Burke eyes American trip for Shayem after Thoroughbred success

Karl Burke is eyeing a trip to America with Shayem after he denied the fast-finishing favourite Talk Of New York in the HKJC World Pool Thoroughbred Stakes.

Having finished third behind Wednesday's Sussex Stakes one-two Bow Echo and Gstaad in the St James's Palace at Royal Ascot, this Group Three contest looked a gilt-edged opportunity for Charlie Appleby's Talk Of New York to get back on the winning trail and he was priced up accordingly as the 2-5 market leader.

But while his stablemate Catullus was deployed in a pacemaking role in an attempt to ensure a sound gallop, the favourite was still keen during the early exchanges under William Buick and it then took him a while to find top gear once asked to close the gap.

Karl Burke's Shayem - winner of the Listed Sir Henry Cecil Stakes at Newmarket three weeks ago - was always in the prime position behind Catullus and after grabbing the lead racing inside the final half-furlong, he had enough in hand to keep Talk Of New York at bay by half a length in the hands of Clifford Lee.

"We don't have to lead, but we knew Billy (Loughnane, riding Catullus) was going to go off a nice gallop and Cliff was the only one really to keep tabs on the leader," said Burke.

"Last year, you would have said that he was a soft ground horse but he has proven otherwise this year. We had no qualms about the ground or the track as he handled the undulations at Newmarket well.

"Cliff is very good with his fractions. It was a great performance and Abdulrazaq (Mohamdi, owner) will be delighted as he's a homebred horse as well. He's a great supporter of ours from Dubai.

"There is a nice race at Kentucky Downs for him in September and one at Colonial Downs as well. I don't think they are Grade Ones but they are very valuable races and if if we don't go there, we could come back for the Celebration Mile."

Appleby will let the dust settle on Talk Of New York's disappointing defeat before considering his next move.

He said: "At the top of the hill I thought they'd have to go a bit to go past the lead horse because he's no mug and he likes the track. Stretching to the mile was always going to be the undoing of Catullus - stop the clock a furlong out and we were a comfortable winner.

"William said himself, the front two stole a good march on him and they're two sensible horses. We knew that Catullus was not going to see the mile out eventually but Will said 'I was only just getting rolling there the last furlong'

"I'm not using the track as an excuse, I think the winner is sensible and is improving, he's done everything right, got a nice lead from us and used it, and we've gone and finished the race off.

"You could say do we need to step up in trip? Possibly. But he has got to learn to settle a little bit as well - that first furlong he does want to be a little bit aggressive, but I don't think that was really the undoing of the race to be fair. The pace was on and they weren't coming back at the end of the day."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino ‘has lost Uefa’s confidence’ after Fifa chief scraps World Cup sell-off plan
Sports.content:
Uefa has warned Gianni Infantino that his style of leadership cannot continue in demanding a thorough and fundamental review of Fifa’s governance.

In a strongly worded statement that referred to “secret schemes”, “shabby backroom deals” and “faceless individuals”, the Uefa leadership made clear it wants change at the top of Fifa, despite the world governing body’s overnight U-turn in abandoning Infantino’s plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other competitions.

While stopping short of calling for Infantino to resign, Uefa’s leadership is understood to be determined that he should not be permitted to survive a crisis of his own making, a view that is shared by many of the biggest football governing bodies across the world. Leading European officials are already understood to have begun the process of identifying a candidate to stand against Infantino in next year’s Fifa presidential election, which will continue over the next few days.

Uefa’s statement made clear that under the leadership of president Aleksander Ceferin, who succeeded in getting all 55 member associations to support a World Cup boycott last Thursday, it will continue to push for change.

“We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game,” the statement read. “We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

“It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, Uefa will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current Fifa leadership has not only lost Uefa’s confidence, but also that of many other members of the football family.”

Uefa went on to criticise Infantino directly, saying he has failed to deliver on pledges he made to be transparent and accountable before he was first elected president in 2016.

View image in fullscreen Aleksander Ceferin and Gianni Infantino, pictured together in 2024. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

The Football Association backed Uefa and, in a statement, said: “We stand shoulder to shoulder with our European colleagues and fully support the collective view. We oppose Fifa’s plans – the Fifa World Cup belongs to football and always will.”

Infantino had been expected to be re-elected unopposed for a third full term at next March’s Fifa Congress in Rabat, but while he is determined to stay on the 56-year-old could now face a challenger. While he has already secured more than 200 letters of support from member associations endorsing his re-election campaign they can be withdrawn, and the deadline for other candidates to announce an intention to stand is not until 18 November.

The Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi is favoured by many in Europe, but appears reluctant to stand and is also chair of powerful lobby group, European Football Clubs. Other potential candidates include Victor Montagliani, the Canadian who is the president of North American confederation Concacaf, and the Asian Football Confederation president Salman al-Khalifa, who lost narrowly to Infantino in the 2016 Fifa election.

Uefa’s statement used Infantino’s own words from his initial election campaign 10 years ago against him. “When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of Fifa’s Member Associations to elect him as their president in 2016, he said, ‘Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in Uefa. You will have to play a part every day in the life of Fifa,’ before telling the assembled stakeholders, ‘The money of Fifa is your money. It’s not the money of the Fifa president. It’s your money. You are the national associations, and the money of Fifa has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.’

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through were anything but transparent. And with reserves standing at over $5bn, he has also failed to use associations’ money for the benefit of the game.”

Uefa also called for an immediate overhaul of Fifa’s system of financial distribution, the Fifa Forward programme in which all 211 member associations receive the same central payment from Fifa over each four-year cycle. Infantino had claimed that selling 20% of a new commercial company – Fifa Forward Enterprise – to private investors would enable them to increase the Fifa Forward payments from $8m over the next four-year cycle to $20m, as well as a one-off $20m bonus for signing up to the scheme.

Handing out millions of dollars to tiny nations has been widely criticised as a system of patronage designed to keep Infantino in office, while the $20m bonus on offer for associations who signed up by a deadline of 19 September was condemned.

View image in fullscreen The Fifa logo in front of its headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland. Gianni Infantino’s senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro and chief operating officer Kevin Lamour opposed his plan. Photograph: Arnd Wiegmann/Reuters

“Uefa will begin work immediately with partners and stakeholders all over the world and right across the game to propose a new way of distributing resources through the existing Fifa Forward programme,” its statement continued. “We must start to use some of that money that is sat idle in Fifa’s bank account to deliver the kick start that the grassroots and the wider game need in each of the 211 countries of Fifa. But we don’t need to sell off the family silver to pay for it.

“This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in Fifa has only just begun.”

Sports.title: Women’s football continues to be used as a pawn in Gianni Infantino’s Fifa tenure | Suzanne Wrack
Sports.content:
Despite not having been deemed worthy of more than a single mention in Fifa’s 25-page sales deck to its 211 member associations on its doomed proposal to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, now very expensive waste paper, it was women’s football that had found itself on the frontline in the fight for the “soul of football”.

Uefa’s statement that European national teams would not “participate in any Fifa competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that Fifa will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership”, was a bold, necessary and effective declaration of war against the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino.

However, with the Under-20 Women’s World Cup being held in Poland next month; the Under-17 Women’s World Cup and Uefa’s qualifying playoffs for the senior tournament both beginning in October; and the big one, the Women’s World Cup itself, taking place in Brazil next summer, women’s tournaments would have been the first test cases had a boycott gone ahead.

There was no further detail on the FA’s plans for England’s two-legged World Cup playoff against Greece, but Uefa’s call for a boycott would have had an impact on the women’s game in September.

A boycott of the Women’s World Cup would have been catastrophic and yet that was the likely consequence of Infantino’s deadline. The 2023 Women’s World Cup was the first to break even after generating more than $570m (£424m) in revenue and Fifa said in May 2025 it is targeting $1bn in revenue from the 2027 edition.

The women’s game is so desperately reliant on international competition for accelerating its growth that the knock-on impact of having no World Cup would have set progress back far more than four years.

However, Uefa was not wrong in its stance and the subsequent collapse of Infantino’s masterplan after the almighty fallout from demonstrates as much. It was not European football’s governing body that engineered the timeframe that put women’s football on the frontline and it was correct not to exclude women’s football, or youth football, from its arsenal in the fight back against Infantino’s attempt to steamroller through his plans.

View image in fullscreen England’s dream of avenging their World Cup final defeat in 2023 was thrown into doubt by Gianni Infantino’s proposals. Photograph: Zac Goodwin/PA

The blame for the threat posed by a boycott on women’s football lay squarely at the feet of Gianni “I have four daughters” Infantino, who was praised in February by Jill Ellis, Fifa’s chief football officer and twice a World Cup-winning coach, for his “commitment to accelerating the women’s game and increasing women’s influence in shaping its future” and under whose leadership “investment has moved from rhetoric to action”.

To an extent Ellis is right – Infantino is the Fifa president who has done the most for the women’s game. But when his predecessor is Sepp Blatter, a man who said in 2004 that “tighter shorts” was the way to get more people watching the women’s game, the bar is staggeringly low.

Yes, under Infantino Fifa has invested more in the women’s game than ever before, but it has been a pawn in his tenure: initially useful for showing just how progressive and in tune with modern society he and Fifa are, and now useful because it presents an opportunity for medium- to long-term financial gain as one of the fastest growing and least‑tapped areas of the game.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Step behind the rhetoric and handouts and Infantino’s real attitude to the women’s game is evident. In 2023 Sky News reported the Fifa president had left the Women’s World Cup for Tahiti after less than a week, before returning later in the tournament. By contrast, he went to at least some part of every one of the 64 games of the 2022 men’s World Cup and at times appeared at two a day during the latest men’s edition despite the huge environmental impact of using a private jet.

View image in fullscreen The 2027 Women’s World Cup in Brazil starts in less than 11 months. Photograph: Athit Perawongmetha/Reuters

Perhaps Infantino waited until the beginning of a new four-year men’s World Cup cycle to try to limit the impact of any backlash on the showpiece event, but in doing so he added to the pile of evidence demonstrative of real attitude towards women’s football, with women’s edition of the tournament on the imminent horizon.

It would have been oddly fitting, then, if the women’s game had become the sun that melted his Icarus wings. Luckily, women’s football didn’t have to pay that costly price. However, this episode must act as a warning, both to those who care about the development of the women’s game and its future and those who care about the future of the men’s game.

The reality is that the European Super League debacle and this latest and most blatant of attempts to hand the wealth of football to private finance vultures show that private finance will keep coming back as they search for ways to get a piece of the pie.

Sports.title: Have you ever switched allegiance as a football fan? You are not alone | Luke McLaughlin
Sports.content:
“I was fanatically pro-German when the Germans were here to protect us against the Americans, and now that Americans are here to protect us against the Germans, I am fanatically pro-American … you and your country will have no more loyal partisan in Italy than me – but only as long as you remain in Italy.”

This passage from Joseph Heller’s Catch-22 – as an old Italian man explains the logic behind his fickle wartime expedience to a naive American soldier – plays with the question of what constitutes true strength. Universally perceived as weak, Italy are in fact the strongest nation in the second world war, according to the old man. And that, sort of, explains my feelings on football fandom.

My dad was passionate about cricket and chess. But I was a football-mad kid, and he dutifully escorted my brother and I to watch West Ham v Nottingham Forest at Upton Park in November 1987. Dad naturally knew about Brian Clough and correctly predicted it would be an entertaining game: the hosts won 3-2.

After that ridiculously exciting day as a 10-year-old, and despite living in south London, I became a Forest supporter, despite photos existing of me in Everton and Tottenham kits earlier in childhood. My mid-1980s decision to support Everton, for clarity, had been pure, unadulterated glory-hunting. Why I then decided to switch to Tottenham, I don’t recall, but it may have had something to do with Paul Gascoigne’s unique ability.

Geographically I should have supported Crystal Palace or Millwall given I was brought up between their grounds: I vividly remember visiting the Den with a Swindon-supporting schoolmate during the era of Terry Hurlock.

As a cricket fan, I have stuck with Middlesex since childhood, but there was never any familial impetus to support a football club. My brother became an Arsenal fan and when I was old enough to regularly attend games alone I started following Forest around London, including a draw at the Den in 1993-94 marred by post-match violence after a Stan Collymore equaliser ended Millwall’s playoff hopes.

When Forest sank into the doldrums after the magical mid-90s, I started to pay less attention to them in classic fairweather-fan fashion. Recently, when living in Somerset, I dabbled with being a Yeovil supporter. Now back living in London I am a regular patron at the Den and have begun to follow Millwall’s results more than Forest’s.

It’s not unusual to support an overseas club either, and after a formative experience watching Napoli lose to Chelsea in 2012 a passion for the Italian club emerged. I’ve visited Naples several times, made good friends there and seen a few games. The most memorable trip was in May 2023 when the Serie A title was sealed under Luciano Spalletti. I didn’t have a ticket but ultimately didn’t need one: the entire city was electrified by their (our) third scudetto.

View image in fullscreen ‘As a teenage follower of Forest, I felt my personal fortunes were linked to the club’s.’ Bayern Munich’s Jürgen Klinsmann takes on Steve Chettle in 1996. Photograph: Lee Beskeen/Action

For some people switching, or even mixing, football allegiances remains taboo. Devoted supporters of a single club may regard my experience as a sign of weakness, or at least exceptional fickleness. But “fan” is short for “fanatic”, and I am no longer convinced so much emotional energy should be invested in supporting any club. Why, after all, would I associate my happiness and sense of fulfilment with something I can’t control? Was the obvious and sustained misery of Arsenal fans as they edged nervously to the Premier League title worth the payoff? Perhaps it was, but there is clearly something unhealthy in that level of obsession.

It is possible, after all, to be too emotionally invested in a certain outcome for your own wellbeing. As an avid teenage follower of Forest, I felt my personal fortunes were linked to the club’s. I regarded one particularly inept late-90s defeat by Wimbledon as a personal tragedy that raised serious questions about my future happiness. I still love football – I am just more ambivalent to its outcomes.

Not only is it acceptable to switch allegiance, it actually makes more sense to base your support on what’s going on in your life at the time. If professional athletes can represent more than one country, let alone several clubs, why shouldn’t fans switch teams?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The disparity between mercenary players and loyal fans grows ever bigger and more grotesque. The players earn obscene amounts of money, and wield a disproportionate amount of power, but often show zero loyalty to a club and its fans when a better offer appears. How can any of this make sense for the lifelong supporter?

And being a diehard fan can be a compromising position in so many ways, frequently leading to defending the indefensible, from unethical petro-state sportwashing and financial doping to obvious on-field foul play and even spying. If you are a glory-hunting Manchester City devotee with a hidden Manchester United-supporting past, or have ever done a football-supporting switcheroo of any kind, do not be ashamed. There is help available. There are people who understand.

Since becoming a regular attendee at Millwall, I’ve enjoyed watching matches with one of my oldest friends and his son. A tight, noisy, old-fashioned ground, no video assistant referee, close to home … have I finally become a real fan?

As long as I live in London I will enjoy following Millwall … with Forest and Napoli thrown in. Not forgetting Dulwich Hamlet. Should I ever return to Somerset, though, I’ll be Yeovil till I die.

Sports.title: Marketing stunt or ‘extraordinary’ transfer? Ravenna fans ride wave of the Ronaldinho Effect
Sports.content:
On a scorching summer afternoon in Ravenna, a city far better known for its fifth-century Byzantine mosaics and Dante’s tomb than for footballing glory, eyes are peeled in the historic centre for one of world football’s most recognisable figures – a man who featured in the World Cup final half-time show alongside Madonna and Ronaldo: Ronaldo de Assis Moreira, better known as Ronaldinho.

“We haven’t seen him yet,” four Ravenna supporters sitting at a cafe say with dry irony as they flip through La Gazzetta dello Sport, Italy’s famous pink sports daily. They are undeniably sceptical, viewing the signing as a purely commercial operation, yet deep down they still harbour the dream of seeing the 2005 Ballon d’Or and 2002 World Cup winner wear their yellow and red shirt.

It is a small, surreal glimpse into the whirlwind that has engulfed this quiet corner of Emilia-Romagna, thanks to the business instinct of Ignazio Cipriani. Heir to the Venetian hospitality dynasty behind the renowned Harry’s Bar, Cipriani took over the club in 2024 when they were in Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football. A native of Ravenna, he is the grandson of Raul Gardini, the Italian chemicals tycoon and sailor who steered Il Moro di Venezia to the 1992 America’s Cup final.

In his first year as president, Cipriani oversaw victory in the Serie D Cup and promotion to the professional ranks of Serie C. But that is merely the first step in a long ascent, he says: “It’s not a provocation. Serie A is the goal I declared from day one because I intend to reach it. And the Champions League remains the ultimate horizon we want to walk towards, step by step. I made this statement because I like working with my back against the wall: when you have no way out, you are forced to find solutions instead of excuses. I prefer to remove every alibi from the beginning.”

And this summer, Cipriani pulled off a surprise move – so surprising that anyone reading the headlines assumed it was a prank: bringing the 46-year-old Ronaldinho back as a player.

View image in fullscreen Ronaldinho holds up a Ravenna top with Ignazio Cipriani, the club president, after the surprise move was announced in Miami in June. Photograph: Rebecca Blackwell/AP

“We met through Lorenzo Tonetti and Ariedo Braida,” Cipriani says, “two people who worked for over 20 years at AC Milan and had Ronaldinho as a player. The idea of involving him was a dream I cultivated as soon as I bought the club. Thanks to Lorenzo and Ariedo, we met, started talking, and a genuine friendship grew. From that relationship came many ideas for the club’s growth. And to the question everyone is asking, I am happy to answer: Ronaldinho will wear the Ravenna shirt as a player, and he will try – maybe scoring the last goal of his career with us!”

Meanwhile, a dedicated website has already put a special-edition shirt on sale featuring the “R10” logo – the Brazilian’s personal brand – which sold out within a few hours. It represents a striking collision of high-end global branding, small-town football, and brilliantly executed marketing stunt.

“If someone had told me three years ago that Ronaldinho was coming to Ravenna, I would have sent them straight to the psychiatric ward,” says Fabio laughing, a lifelong supporter. “The night the news broke, international headlines everywhere read ‘Ronaldinho to Ravenna’. It was an extraordinary operation.”

Ravenna is no footballing giant. Plagued by bankruptcies in 2001 and 2012, the club has spent decades bouncing around the lower tiers, with seven seasons in Serie B the highest point. Historically a volleyball stronghold, the football scene was accustomed to modest budgets and regional rivalries.

View image in fullscreen Ronaldinho will be aiming to wow the crowds at Ravenna’s Stadio Bruno Benelli this season. Photograph: Roberto Salomone/The Guardian

“Ronaldinho is a unique icon,” Cipriani says. “His way of playing made my generation fall in love with the game. We want him today to make the next generation of fans, in Italy and around the world, fall in love with Ravenna . It’s not just a visibility stunt; it’s about building a bridge between different eras of football and growing a truly global fanbase around it.”

To support this ambitious sporting and industrial project, the club is working with the municipality to renovate the Stadio Bruno Benelli, increasing its capacity beyond 6,300. But the president’s ultimate dream is a new multi-purpose venue open seven days a week, featuring retail spaces, concert facilities, and an integrated Hotel Cipriani linked to the city’s international tourism expansion.

For Ravenna’s mayor, Alessandro Barattoni, the arrival of a world-famous figure fits neatly into a broader strategy to promote the city globally. In recent years, Ravenna has been expanding its international reach beyond traditional beach tourism and commercial ports. The city is enjoying renewed ties with the Anglo-Saxon world, highlighted by a recent visit from the British royal family and the opening of the Lord Byron Museum.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Ronaldinho brings a whole new level of global fame,” Barattoni says. “When the news broke, my phone exploded with messages from former schoolmates. For younger kids today, he might be someone to discover on YouTube, but the fascination remains intact.” With a smile, the mayor adds that, schedule permitting, he would be delighted to personally guide Ronaldinho on a tour of the city’s cultural heritage.

However, Barattoni is quick to clarify the institution’s role: “Our common ground with the club is internationalisation: bringing Ravenna’s image to the world. Ronaldinho has been a global ambassador for countless brands. There is an overarching project that can bring great visibility to the team and allow the city to showcase its initiatives beyond standard routes.” He adds: “Even before Ronaldinho’s arrival, the club did a fantastic job engaging younger generations. The average age in the stands is lower, more vibrant, and more engaged than ever before. A genuine sense of community is forming.”

View image in fullscreen Alessandro Barattoni, the mayor of Ravenna, is confident the Ronaldinho transfer will be positive for the Italian city. Photograph: Roberto Salomone/The Guardian

Yet, fears of a hyper-commercialised image linger among traditional supporters. In the Curva Mero, such marketing moves are approached with caution. “There is a certain reluctance among some factions,” Fabio admits. “Modern football pushes values that many don’t share: rising ticket prices, losing accessibility for lower-income families. As a result, visibility and marketing stunts risk being viewed sideways.”

Cipriani demonstrates an acute awareness of these dynamics: “Without roots, no global project makes sense,” the president says. “Ravenna is not a brand we are building from scratch; it’s a history and an identity that existed before us. Tradition isn’t a brake on ambition: it’s the foundation. A club without its people is worth nothing.”

“I’m 50 years old and I’ve been coming to the stadium since my school days,” says Giovanni, another fan. “I’m rediscovering the enthusiasm of the past. If it takes an icon like Ronaldinho and a local entrepreneur to make us dream of Serie A, then so be it. The important thing is never to forget the people in the stands.”

Riding the wave of the “Ronaldinho Effect”, the season-ticket campaign has just launched with a target of selling 2,800. Ticket prices have risen by an average of about 12%, with variations across different stadium sections.

For now, Ravenna is soaking up a dizzying, galvanising atmosphere. On the pitch, the club is assembling a squad to win the league; off it, the city awaits 20 August, when Ronaldinho is expected to appear during a three-day summer festival in nearby Marina di Ravenna, organised in signature Cipriani style.

Sports.title: Rangers held by Dundee United to kick off McInnes era and Scottish Premiership
Sports.content:
Thelo Aasgaard earned Derek McInnes his first point as Rangers manager as they fought back for a 1-1 draw against Dundee United.

Lachlan Rose struck the first goal of the Premiership season to give United a half-time lead at Tannadice.

Rangers lacked control in possession in the opening period but they looked more threatening after the break and Aasgaard finished brilliantly in the 56th minute. They could not build on the equaliser, though, as United soon stemmed the tide of pressure.

View image in fullscreen Dundee United’s Lachlan Rose celebrates after opening the scoring. Photograph: Russell Cheyne/Reuters

Jesse Randall should have won the game for the home side with eight minutes left when substitute Daniel Bennie’s swerving pass put the New Zealand international clean through on goal. However, the winger totally lacked conviction as he dinked a shot straight into goalkeeper Ivor Pandur’s hands.

McInnes named Youssef Chermiti on the bench in his first team selection with Ryan Naderi handed a role on the right of Rangers’ attack, and Pandur, Ben Godfrey, Cammy Devlin and Lawrence Shankland making their debuts.

There were only two Scots in the two starting lineups but both led their teams, former Falkirk midfielder Dylan Tait wearing the armband for United and Shankland the new Rangers captain.

The former Hearts striker was the first to threaten with a flick that drew a reaction stop from Jack Walton, but the home goalkeeper’s only other first-half save came from a Naderi header which looked like it was slightly off target. Rose and Zac Sapsford got in behind for the home side but could not get shots on target and the Rangers defence was busy on other occasions as United worked the ball into the box.

View image in fullscreen Derek McInnes began his time at Rangers with a hard-fought 1-1 draw at Dundee United on the opening day of the season. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Dujon Sterling and Mohamed Diomande were off target from outside the box for Rangers, before the hosts made the breakthrough in the 38th minute. Rangers centre-back Emmanuel Fernandez was out of position as Sapsford dummied Randall’s low cross and Rose watched in delight as his left-foot effort spun off the post and over the line.

Chermiti and Dan Neil came on for Naderi and Djeidi Gassama as McInnes tried to affect the game at half-time and his side immediately looked more threatening.
