Quick Guide Bellingham watches Birmingham beat Barça in friendly Show Jude Bellingham returned to St Andrew's as a spectator to see Birmingham City beat Barcelona on penalties in a pre-season friendly. The England and Real Madrid midfielder (pictured) emerged from Birmingham's academy, making his first-team debut at 16 years old before joining Borussia Dortmund in 2020. August Priske put Birmingham ahead in the 31st minute, but teenage Barça striker Hamza Abdelkarim levelled from the penalty spot before half-time. Abdelkarim struck again on the hour, reacting fastest after Roony Bardghji's shot was saved. Jhon Solis responded for the hosts, volleying home in the 68th minute. The game ended 2-2 after 90 minutes, with Birmingham keeper James Beadle saving twice and 17-year-old Barcelona defender Jordi hitting the crossbar. The shootout ended 3-2 to Birmingham as the hosts enjoyed a memorable victory over an admittedly inexperienced Barcelona line-up. Guardian sport Photograph: Nigel French/PA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Aasgaard forced an excellent diving save from Walton before the Norway international levelled moments later. Shankland’s physical presence caused problems as United were made to defend another high ball and Aasgaard took an excellent touch to take out Joshua Rawlins before firing a left-foot strike into the top corner from 16 yards.

Rangers could not keep up the momentum, and Randall squandered a glorious chance to mark his league debut with a famous winner. Chermiti almost made the home side pay but Walton stopped the striker’s effort with his feet before home substitute Idjessi Metsoko delivered a weak effort straight at Pandur from a decent opportunity.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s title defence: keeping tired players fit and the Vinícius question
Sports.content:
After beating MK Dons 3-0 in a training-ground friendly last weekend, Arsenal truly begin their pre-season programme against Girona on Saturday evening. It marks a return to action for the Premier League champions, who will want to show their success last season was not a one-off.

Retaining the English title is incredibly difficult if you are not Manchester City. No other club has done it since Manchester United won three in succession from 2007 to 2009. Chelsea have done it once, Liverpool have not managed it for more than 40 years, and it is the best part of a century since Arsenal retained the crown. Mikel Arteta faces a sizeable challenge.

Reaching a second successive Champions League final will not be simple either. Manchester City in 2021-22 are the only one of England’s previous five finalists who made it as far as the semi-finals the next season. With the Premier League stronger than ever, competing on two fronts has never been tougher. Transfer business may improve Arsenal’s chances, though their spending has been modest to this point. More than half of the £79m spent was on making Piero Hincapié’s loan permanent.

Elsewhere Arsenal have replaced Leandro Trossard with Christos Tzolis, a Greek winger, from Club Brugge. Seven years younger than the Belgian, his arrival is a logical move in future-proofing the squad. However, the left side of Arsenal’s attack would be elevated to truly elite level if they could secure reported target Vinícius Júnior. The on-field argument speaks for itself. Vinícius made 92 carries of at least five metres that ended with him either taking a shot (49) or creating a chance (43) last season, the most of anyone in Europe’s top five leagues. Open-play threat, for a side that has often relied on set pieces, would be considerably increased.

Those holding the purse strings at Arsenal may have pause for thought. Capology’s wage data estimates that Vinícius is the joint-third highest paid player in Europe’s top five leagues, earning in excess of £100,000 a week more than anyone at his potential new club. Would Arsenal be willing to rewrite their wage structure? They should expect calls from the agents of their current players if they are. In this sense, Bradley Barcola, with whom they have also been linked, makes a more plausible target. The issue there would be competition from Liverpool, who are in far greater need of wingers.

This is the test facing Andrea Berta, Arsenal’s sporting director. Improving a squad that is already one of the best around is not easy. When Berta’s arrived last year, the club’s primary targets were said to be Alexander Isak and Benjamin Sesko, both of whom joined rivals instead. The pool of players who could add something significant to Arteta’s options is drying up.

Keeping existing players fit may be more beneficial than enhancing the squad. Arsenal did well to win the league given only a handful of clubs had players that missed more games. Kai Havertz was reportedly their top earner before Bukayo Saka signed a contract extension in February, but he only started seven league games. The captain, Martin Ødegaard, was also unavailable for spells, meaning he and Saka started only 10 Premier League matches together in 2025-26. One of them coincided with the only game for which Declan Rice was injured (the 4-1 home win over Aston Villa), another (another home win, 2-1 against Brighton) when he started at right-back.

View image in fullscreen Mikel Arteta indulges in a bit of training-ground banter with first-team coach Miguel Molina in Girona. Photograph: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

This meant Arteta was rarely able to give key men a breather. Arsenal have five of the Premier League’s top 20 players for club minutes in all competitions since the start of last season. Granted, the goalkeeper David Raya is one of them. But their outfield players with more than 4,200 minutes were Rice (4,456 minutes, the 11th most for a Premier League club), Martín Zubimendi (4,298, 15th), William Saliba (4,254, 17th) and Gabriel Magalhães (4,210, 19th), all vital components of the side’s spine.

Saliba also played 795 minutes for France, pushing him past 5,000 minutes before his World Cup was prematurely ended by a back injury that looks likely to sideline him for some time. It is remarkable Rice was able to play 1,026 minutes for England on top of his Arsenal commitments, not least as he has managed nerve pain in a hamstring throughout 2026.

This workload clearly impacted his ability to contribute at his best for Thomas Tuchel this summer, and that will be a concern for Arteta. With Viktor Gyökeres also clocking up plenty of playing time for Sweden, Arsenal have six players with at least 4,400 minutes for club and country since the start of last August.

This may have been a factor in Arsenal opting for a relatively low-key pre-season. They visited Asia last summer, but the trip to Catalonia to play Girona is the furthest they will travel this year. Arsenal also have games in Dublin (against Real Betis) and Cardiff (the Community Shield against City) sandwiching home friendlies against Borussia Dortmund and Como.

With players still recovering from their World Cup exertions, it may be some time before we see the true Arsenal. A combination of fatigue, injuries and potential squad additions means the process could take far longer than would be ideal.

Sports.title: Inter make new approach to Liverpool for Curtis Jones with £30m offer likely
Sports.content:
Inter have made another approach for Curtis Jones and are willing to raise their offer for the Liverpool midfielder to €35m (£30m). The Italian champions had a €25m bid for the 25-year-old rejected in June by Liverpool, who value their homegrown player at closer to €40m.

Quick Guide Bellingham watches Birmingham beat Barça in friendly Show Jude Bellingham returned to St Andrew's as a spectator to see Birmingham City beat Barcelona on penalties in a pre-season friendly. The England and Real Madrid midfielder (pictured) emerged from Birmingham's academy, making his first-team debut at 16 years old before joining Borussia Dortmund in 2020. August Priske put Birmingham ahead in the 31st minute, but teenage Barça striker Hamza Abdelkarim levelled from the penalty spot before half-time. Abdelkarim struck again on the hour, reacting fastest after Roony Bardghji's shot was saved. Jhon Solis responded for the hosts, volleying home in the 68th minute. The game ended 2-2 after 90 minutes, with Birmingham keeper James Beadle saving twice and 17-year-old Barcelona defender Jordi hitting the crossbar. The shootout ended 3-2 to Birmingham as the hosts enjoyed a memorable victory over an admittedly inexperienced Barcelona line-up. Guardian sport Photograph: Nigel French/PA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Intermediaries representing Inter have made fresh contact with Liverpool this week and outlined their willingness to go to €35m for a player who has only one year remaining on his contract at Anfield. Whether Liverpool accept that sum is doubtful, but a deal for Jones to leave his boyhood club does appear to be edging closer.

Jones has been unable to establish himself as a regular starter at Liverpool and cut a frustrated figure at times last season under Arne Slot. He was also involved in a row with Dominik Szoboszlai after Wednesday’s win over Wrexham in New York, seemingly over not being handed the captain’s armband when Szoboszlai was substituted during the second half of the friendly.

Sports.title: Chelsea fined £10m and given suspended transfer ban by FA over agent breaches
Sports.content:
Chelsea have been fined £10m by the FA and served with a suspended transfer ban for multiple violations of transfer rules during the Roman Abramovich era.

The sanction reflects a similar punishment handed to the Blues by the Premier League earlier this year after the club were found to have used unlicensed agents and sought to obscure the nature of their transfer dealings between 2009 and 2022. Deals involving Chelsea legends Samuel Eto’o, Eden Hazard and Willian were among those found to have breached the rules. The commission originally handed down a stronger sanction that would have given Chelsea a suspended six-point deduction, but it was overturned after an appeal by the club.

The offences were self-reported by Chelsea when new ownership entered Stamford Bridge in 2022 and the disciplinary panel praised the club for their actions and cooperation through the hearing. Chelsea, who are also operating under a settlement agreement with Uefa, said they had “worked openly and transparently with all regulators” and were “pleased to confirm that this brings all regulatory proceedings against the club to a close”.

Written reasons published by the FA show the independent commission took a very dim view of the Abramovich-era administration, saying their rule-breaking showed “a shameful and arrogant disregard for the rules of the game … which has done so much to bring the game of football in general, and the name of CFC into disrepute”. They also said, however, that there were aspects of the case brought by the FA that caused them “particular concern”.

While praising the FA’s cooperation on the case, the commission criticised the governing body for both failing to charge individuals related to the misdemeanours and for requesting that a sporting sanction should not be applied as punishment. After a submission by the Premier League, which also argued against a sporting sanction, Chelsea appealed against the commission’s original sanction and the six-point deduction was replaced with a suspended two-window ban on registering new players. While the commission had originally argued Chelsea had sought and gained a sporting advantage from their actions, the appeal board found that there was insufficient evidence to show that any advantage had actually been achieved.

“Chelsea’s lawyers performed a masterclass in non-adversarial diplomacy with both the FA and the Premier League,” said Stefan Borson, a football finance expert who is head of sport at the law firm McCarthy Denning.

“Even where the FA’s independent panel disagreed with the position presented by the FA and Chelsea, it still found a way to discount a 15-point deduction starting point down to a six-point suspended penalty. Ultimately, even that was appealed away, leaving Chelsea to pay a final meagre fine out of its retained escrow from Abramovich’s proceeds.”

Quick Guide Mudryk cleared to resume playing Show Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk can return to playing immediately after the Football Association and the World Anti-Doping Agency “resolved his appeal” against a ban for failing a doping test. The Ukrainian was suspended for four years after failing a drug test which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance, in 2024. Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport while changes to Wada procedures in the interim mean that had his failed test produced the same result now, charges would not have been brought. The FA said: “Changes have been made … which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk’s sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no anti-doping rule violations [ADRVs] would have resulted. Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, the FA and Mr Mudryk have now – with the agreement of Wada – resolved the appeal proceedings. “As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the ADRVs charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect.” PA Media Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The Premier League and the FA had been examining tens of millions of pounds in secret payments made by offshore companies that were owned by Abramovich. Details of the transactions were uncovered as part of Cyprus Confidential, an investigation by the Guardian and international media partners, based on a leak of data from Cypriot financial services firms that the Russian oligarch used to manage his vast fortunes.

Deals revealed by the leak included apparent off-book payments to Hazard’s agent and an associate of the title-winning manager Antonio Conte.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Documents published as part of the finding offer a rare insight into the inner workings of Chelsea’s transfer policy during the tenure of Abramovich. They refer to internal conversations at Chelsea about the purchase of Willian in 2013, a deal agreed at the last minute, after the Brazilian had apparently been set to join London rivals Tottenham. According to the documents, an unnamed senior figure at Chelsea felt that to lose Willian was “not good” and that to lose him to Tottenham was “adding insult to injury”.

In its argument, the FA said the unnamed individual may have “loved the power associated with having a bottomless pocket when it came to acquiring players of great quality and/or with great potential, but to seek to suggest that there was no intention to obtain a sporting advantage is stretching our credulity beyond reasonable limits”.

The rulings published by the FA also reveal for the first time that BlueCo, the consortium that bought Chelsea from Abramovich, reached a multi-million pound settlement with HM Revenue & Customs relating to transactions dating back to 2011. The size of the settlement is redacted in the FA’s case against Chelsea but the appeal board’s decision indicated that the club repaid at least £1.35m.

The FA said that the entirety of Chelsea’s £10m fine will be invested into grassroots football.

Sports.title: Arsenal warned over ‘biggest red herring in history’ amid growing Vinicius Jr reports
Sports.content:
Arsenal fans have been warned not to get carried away in the club's pursuit of Vinicius Junior.

The Brazil superstar continues to be linked with a move to North London amid uncertainty surrounding his Real Madrid future.



2 Vinicius joined Real Madrid in 2018, but his future at the Bernabeu remains unclear Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands there remains a standoff between Vinicius and Madrid over a new contract and that the Gunners are very much interested.

Some reports have gone as far as to say Arsenal are ready to strike personal terms with the 26-year-old if he decides not to extend his contract in Spain.

talkSPORT reported last week that the Gunners were weighing up an approach for Vinicius though viewed him as an option rather than their top target.



Vinicius 'trying to up the ante'

And talkSPORT's Rory Jennings has suggested the transfer would be "the biggest signing in Premier League history" were it to go through.

Conversely, Transfer Insiders host Rickie Haywood-Williams believes the situation could be a huge misdirection.



"I think this is the biggest red herring in history in terms of live transfers," he said on talkSPORT. "Because I feel like Vinicius Jr has been trying to get a new contract at Real Madrid for the last couple of years.

"In that time, they’ve signed [Kylian] Mbappe – Mbappe is on incredible money and he [Vinicius] obviously is going to want parity with that or somewhere close, and I think he’s using the Premier League as a bit of a bargaining chip to try and up the ante on his money, to try and get a bigger contract.



"What do you reckon?" he posed to co-host Dan Bardell, who responded: "Surely, though, despite the Arsenal interest, surely he’s going to get a big contract anyway – because they’re [Madrid] not going to let him run down his contract and go for a free.

"I think they’ve said – it’s quite well known – that if he doesn’t sign a contract this summer, they will look to sell him and it would still be an incredible amount of money."

Vinicius has just one year left to run on his deal at the Bernabeu, meaning he would be available on a free transfer next summer.

2 Vinicius recorded five goal contributions for Brazil at this summer's World Cup Credit: Getty



A hefty price tag

Madrid signed the 26-year-old from Flamengo back in 2018 for a reported £39m.

Transfermarkt currently values the two-time Champions League winner at almost £120m.

Indeed, South American football expert Jon Cotterill recently told talkSPORT Arsenal would have to be prepared to pay more than £100m to land Vinicius.

The Gunners have only ever spent that kind of money on a player once before, signing Declan Rice for £105m from West Ham three years ago.



As things stand, Arsenal appear to be the only candidates to secure Vinicius' services in the event he turns down a new deal at Madrid.

Liverpool were offered the chance to sign him earlier this summer but decided against pursuing a move.

Sports.title: Chelsea vs Tottenham threatens to boil over within minutes after Conor Gallagher challenge
Sports.content:
Chelsea vs Tottenham threatens to boil over within minutes after Conor Gallagher challenge

There is no such thing as a 'friendly' between Chelsea and Tottenham.

And Blues academy product Conor Gallagher, now of Spurs, knows that better than anyone.

4 Gallagher delivered a classic 'let them know you're there' Down Under Credit: SPURSPLAY

4 Essugo was sent flying Credit: Getty

The two London rivals met in the Sydney Super Cup for a pre-season game on Saturday.

Just ten minutes in, tensions threatened to boil over when Gallagher made a late challenge on Chelsea midfielder Dario Essugo.

The Spurs player was running at speed and slid into a crunching tackle on the Portuguese youngster.

A number of Chelsea players, including Joao Pedro and Wesley Fofana, rushed to confront Gallagher.

Dominic Solanke and Levi Colwill were among those to play peacemakers and prevent it from becoming anything more than handbags.

Gallagher was ultimately shown a yellow card for the challenge.

Moments later, Spurs' record signing Sandro Tonali put them in front, before Estevao quickly equalised for the Blues.

But things later took a turn for the worse for Roberto De Zerbi's side as Kevin Danso was shown a straight red card for denying Joao Pedro a clear goalscoring opportunity.

4 Danso sent Joao Pedro tumbling... Credit: Spursplay

4 ...and left the referee with no option but to produce a red card Credit: Spursplay

Gallagher in the bad books again

Despite coming through the ranks at Chelsea and going on to make 95 first-team appearances, Gallagher has since taken him elsewhere.

After four loan spells away from Stamford Bridge, Gallagher joined Spanish giants Atletico Madrid in the summer of 2024.

However, he was back in the Premier League less than 18 months later, completing what he described as a "very easy" move to Spurs.

Returning to Stamford Bridge for the first time as an opposition player for March's 2-1 defeat, Gallagher was booed by Blues fans as he stepped out in the colours of their London rivals.

Blues and Spurs step up new season prep

A number of summer signings are in action for both clubs in Australia today.

Marco Palestra started for Chelsea, with Spurs including Jan Paul van Hecke, Andy Robertson and Tonali in their starting XI.

This clash is the last match of Spurs' pre-season tour of New Zealand and Australia.

They return to action with a training ground friendly against Getafe next Saturday.

Chelsea, meanwhile, head to Hong Kong to face Juventus on Wednesday.

Sports.title: UEFA issue damning vote of no confidence against Gianni Infantino as FA demand FIFA investigation
Sports.content:
UEFA has released a statement saying it has 'lost confidence' in Gianni Infantino, following his failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

FIFA president Infantino had planned to sell off stakes in football governing body's competitions to private investors, but scrapped the idea in the early hours of Saturday morning amid widespread outrage.

4 Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president is becoming increasingly untenable Credit: Getty

Multiple continental federations were strongly opposed to the project, including UEFA.

European football's governing body warned that its member nations would boycott future FIFA tournaments if the plan went ahead.

Infantino has also seen his inner circle begin to crumble - senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro resigned on Friday, releasing a strongly worded statement opposing the FFE plans.

And now, after the under-fire football chief was forced to pull the plug on his controversial proposal, UEFA has welcomed the decision.

In a statement, UEFA blasted Infantino's plans, and thanked the 'fans, leagues, clubs, players, individuals, associations and confederations that opposed the scheme'.

The European football authority also said the 'current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA’s confidence but also that of many other members of the football family'.

UEFA statement in full “UEFA welcomes FIFA’s decision to withdraw its plan to sell a stake in its competitions – including the World Cup – into private hands. “The proposal was unanimously rejected by UEFA’s national associations and by many other federations and confederations of all sizes around the world, whose job it is to protect football. “UEFA thanks all the fans, leagues, clubs, players, individuals, associations and confederations that opposed the scheme, alongside the many Prime Ministers, Heads of State and commentators who have demonstrated to the FIFA President that football is not for sale. “We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account. “It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA’s confidence but also that of many other members of the football family. “When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA’s Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, “Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA. You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA,” before telling the assembled stakeholders, “The money of FIFA is your money. It’s not the money of the FIFA President. It’s your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.” “On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through was anything but transparent. “And with reserves standing at over $5bn, he has also failed to use associations’ money for the benefit of the game. “UEFA will begin work immediately with partners and stakeholders all over the world and right across the game to propose a new way of distributing resources through the existing FIFA Forward programme. “We must start to use some of that money that is sat idle in FIFA’s bank account to deliver the kick start that the grassroots and the wider game need in each of the 211 countries of FIFA. But we don’t need to sell off the family silver to pay for it. “This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun.”

FA follow suit

The FA followed UEFA with its own statement shortly afterwards, demanding a thorough investigation into FIFA's leadership.

A spokesperson said: “We fully support UEFA’s position.

"It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long - term stewardship of football at its heart”

No way back?

UEFA's damning statement places even more pressure on Infantino's position in charge of FIFA.

4 Infantino's FFE project had intended to raise hundreds of millions of dollars by selling off chunks in the commercial rights of the men's and women's World Cups

His failed FFE proposal faced almost total opposition across the board, with CONCACAF and the AFC joining UEFA in publicly slamming the plans.

With the proposal reliant on FIFA's 211 Member Federations voting it through, the opposition of three continental federations left Infantino facing 143 votes against his pitch.

The FFE was a plan to roll the World Cup's broadcasting, licensing, ticketing and sponsorship into one big company.

20 per cent of it was then going to be sold to private investors, with Infantino in line to make millions.

The private stakeholders would have then got a say in what happened to the World Cup as well, but this will no longer materialise.

Infantino was already under intense scrutiny in his role as FIFA president this summer following the World Cup and the manner of Folarin Balogun's suspended ban.

4 UEFA are headed up by president Aleksander Ceferin Credit: Getty

USA striker Balogun was cleared to play against Belgium in the last 16 after his red card ban was suspended for a year after intervention from US President Donald Trump.

UEFA slammed FIFA's decision at the time, insisting it 'crossed a red line' in a furious statement.

What did Infantino say?

The FIFA president still attempted to defend the project as he climbed down from it in the early hours of Saturday morning.

His statement read: "The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

"And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

"Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.

4 Infantino had already been under pressure for his relationship with the Trump administration Credit: Getty

"Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

"Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support."

Sports.title: Arsene Wenger called out for silence as Gianni Infantino scraps FIFA’s toxic FFE scheme
Sports.content:
Arsene Wenger has been questioned for failing to speak out on Gianni Infantino's failed FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal.

FIFA president Infantino had planned to sell off stakes in the world football governing body's competitions to private investors but scrapped the idea in the early hours of Saturday morning amid widespread outrage.



3 Infantino's FFE project had intended to raise hundreds of millions of dollars by selling off chunks in the commercial rights of the men's and women's World Cups Credit: Getty

Multiple continental federations vehemently rejected the project – with UEFA announcing they would boycott future World Cups if it went ahead.

Infantino has also seen his inner circle begin to crumble: senior advisor Carols Codeiro resigned on Friday, releasing a strongly worded statement opposing the FFE plans.

But one person who has so far stayed silent on the matter is FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development, legendary former Arsenal boss Wenger – much to the surprise of talkSPORT's Tony Cascarino.



Joining Shebahn Aherne on the Weekend Sports Breakfast, the former Chelsea and Republic of Ireland striker said: "The one thing that's really surprised me is Arsene Wenger, who's got a real pivotal role within FIFA and he's obviously been an incredible manager.

"Nothing at all from Arsene Wenger and you'd have felt that he would have [something to say].



"But... the way he's always managed and you always felt he loves the game so much, and what he achieved as a club manager and his role at FIFA – and Arsene's been very, very quiet.

"And it's hard to know exactly where he stands as well – because he'll get questioned, Arsene Wenger."



Aherne suggested Wenger might speak out now Infantino has shelved the highly controversial proposal.

"We don't even know if he might have been against him," Cascarino continued.

"There's certain people... behind the scenes [at FIFA] that have gone, 'Absolutely not, this is not a good idea for football'... selling off the game privately and look, the game makes a lot of money anyway."

3 Burnham has called on Infantino to go Credit: AFP



Infantino's own position in charge of FIFA is bound to come under increased pressure in light of this categorical failure.

And UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called Infantino 'the wrong man' for the job.

Burnham, who was critical of the FFE plans from the outset, told reporters on Friday: "My view is strengthening – this was an outrageous suggestion.

"The idea that it could even be brought forward shows that, in my view, [Infantino] is the wrong man to lead the organisation.



"Let me say this very directly: football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

"The World Cup is not a product; it is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell. Dress the deal up however you like; once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.

3 Wenger has a leading role in FIFA but his thoughts on FFE were never vocalised Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

"Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will."

What did Infantino say?

The FIFA president still attempted to defend the project as he climbed down from it in the early hours of Saturday morning.



His statement read: "The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

"And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

"Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place. Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve.

"As a result, this proposal will not proceed. Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support."

Sports.title: Liverpool’s pre-season win over Wrexham has exposed glaring transfer problem
Sports.content:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola is already being forced to cover for the biggest transfer mistake the club's hierarchy has made.

The Reds ranked Mohamed Salah as the fourth greatest player in Anfield history and yet have little over four weeks to replace him.

7 Mohamed Salah bid an emotional farewell to Liverpool in May, and he is still yet to find a new club Credit: Getty

Two teenagers who haven't played a minute of Premier League football have started at right-wing in each of Iraola's first two games.

That normally wouldn't set any alarm bells ringing in pre-season, especially one that takes place after a World Cup with senior stars on extended breaks.

However, in Liverpool's case, the cavalry won't be belatedly arriving to solve the right-wing issue after Salah's exit at the end of last season.

Against Wrexham, 16-year-old academy talent Joshua Abe was entrusted to start the first half, before Rio Ngumoha took the reins.

The 17-year-old - who made his England debut in June on the right flank - hinted at further developing his game on the opposite side to his favoured left-wing at the start of pre-season.

"Being unpredictable off both sides is key," he said. "Obviously, everyone knows I can play on the left, but on the right I feel like I'm improving and I'm getting better.

"So, yeah, definitely off the left and the right this season."

Ngumoha did indeed score the only goal from the right in the win over Wrexham, with his deflected effort finding the far top corner.

However, the former Cobham starlet is understandably still hugely raw in his new role, having completed just one of his four attempted dribbles while also only managing two touches in the Wrexham box.

Liverpool head coach Iraola said afterwards: "I normally used to try to encourage our wingers to have the ability to play both sides.

7 Liverpool surely had a better plan than to hope Iraola could plug the right wing with a player who favours the left? Credit: AFP

7 Ngumoha showed against Wrexham why he'll need time to develop as a winger who can play both sides Credit: Getty

"I know some of them are more comfortable on one side, but our team is not normally symmetrical," Iraola continued.

"Also, in pre-season, I have to see where they are more comfortable, but in my previous clubs most of the wingers have played both sides."

What was Liverpool's Salah-succession plan before Iraola?

The Reds even surprised Arne Slot when the decision was ultimately made to part ways with the Dutchman at the end of May.

But the club's hierarchy knew months before that Salah's succession plan was being moved up a year after ripping up his contract.

Steven Gerrard told talkSPORT that his dream pick was Michael Olise, but he accepted getting him out of Bayern Munich was fanciful.

Meanwhile, his former Liverpool teammate Michael Owen also suggested Jarrod Bowen prior to the latter remaining at West Ham.

7 Salah is the most notable departure from Liverpool this summer Credit: Getty

Hierarchy shake-up

What Slot's plan would have been for his right side had he stayed at Liverpool is anybody's guess after a myriad of failed experiments.

In games Salah was absent for last season, the Dutchman deployed Jeremie Frimpong and Dominik Szoboszlai at times on the wing - neither of which would have been a long-term solution.

The elephant in the room in terms of Liverpool's transfers is that Michael Edwards, who played a vital role in Salah's arrival under Jurgen Klopp, has stepped down as Fenway Sports Group's (FSG) CEO of football.

Current Reds sporting director Richard Hughes has also been linked with a move to Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal, but remains in charge of incomings and outgoings on Merseyside this summer.

7 Munoz played 18 games for Osasuna last season on the left and made 10 appearances on the right Credit: Getty

Liverpool have indeed been in the market for wingers this summer, having been snubbed in their pursuit of Yan Diomande.

The club then successfully hijacked Newcastle's move for Spain star Victor Munoz in a £34million swoop.

The World Cup winner is predominantly a left winger, but does fit Iraola's bill of being able to operate on the right.

So too is top target Bradley Barcola, for whom talkSPORT understands the Reds are now readying a €100m (around £85m) offer, plus add-ons for the Paris Saint-Germain forward.

The France international has only played on the right flank 37 times in his career and at that price is clearly going to operate in his favoured left position.

7 Over the last two seasons, Barcola has played more than two-thirds of his games on the left wing Credit: Getty

'Square pegs in round holes'

Liverpool explored signing Barcola in 2025 when a price of around €85m (around £73m) was quoted, but reports claimed a desire not to block a pathway for Ngumoha saw their pursuit abandoned.

12 months on, the club may argue that Salah's premature exit has necessitated a rethink, which is why Ngumoha is being tried on the right.

But it would be an almost insurmountable burden for a teenager learning a new role to be expected to replace Salah in only his second full season as a professional, rather than being the chief understudy on both wings to more experienced players.

Peterborough United chairman and Liverpool fan Darragh MacAnthony has admitted he is not enamoured with Barcola's arrival.

He told talkSPORT's Alex Crook: "I'm with Jamie Carragher in the camp. I saw him the other day talking about it. We have like three, four left-wingers already, players who can play there. We need to fill the void left by Salah.

7 Frimpong will be needed at right-back more often than not, with Conor Bradley a long-term absentee Credit: Getty

"Frimpong was meant to help with that, but we know he's had injury issues last year. Not quite what we like to see out wide right when he did play. We need a right winger. It's concerning.

"And we're going out, and we're getting another pacy player who plays on the left the majority of the time.

"So, unless Rio's going to get put on the right, you know, square pegs, round holes, all that kind of thing. I don't know. I don't love it because of the money.

"If he was £60-70 million, and I get it, he's not, you think, okay, it's a no-brainer.

"Then you maybe sell [Cody] Gakpo, and you clear up some space on the left. You still go get a right winger."

MacAnthony added: "Liverpool have got a lot of holes to fill.

"And you've got to start at right wing to fill Mo Salah's departure. So, it does concern me that we're going down this rabbit hole where we might end up paying, I don't know, like the [Florian] Wirtz money; you overpay.

"And then does the player adapt to the Premier League, and is it another bad signing? It's frustrating for me."

Sports.title: Bayern Munich publicly put three players on transfer list including ex-Premier League star
Sports.content:
Joao Palhinha is among three players that Bayern Munich are willing to sell this summer.

Max Eberl, the director of sport at Bayern, has publicly revealed that the players are not part of their plans for the new season.



2 Palhinha is one of three players to be put up for sale by Bayern Credit: Getty

Ismael Saibari was their first summer signing in a reported €50million (£43m) move from PSV Eindhoven.

Bayern then bought Nathaniel Brown, who Manchester United had as a target, in a €55m (£47m) deal with Eintracht Frankfurt.

Players such as Leon Goretzka and Raphael Guerreiro have left at the end of their contracts, and others have gone on loan or permanently.



And according to Eberl, Bayern are keen to let another trio of players depart before the end of the window.

"We have three players we are open to letting go," he explained via @iMiaSanMia on X. "They have no future at Bayern.



"If they want to stay with us, it will be tough because we are not planning with them. Then they won't play a role.

"That's the case with Sacha Boey, Joao Palhinha and Bryan Zaragoza."

Who could Palhinha sign for?

After two solid seasons at Fulham, Palhinha joined Bayern in July 2024 and played a part in their Bundesliga title success that season.



However, he played just 986 minutes across all competitions and then made his way back to the Premier League with Tottenham Hotspur.

The Portuguese midfielder signed on a season-long loan deal, which included an option to buy for £26m.

2 Eberl says the trio do not have a future at the club Credit: Getty

Palhinha played regularly and scored the winner against Everton on the final day to secure the club's status in the top-flight.



Whilst he did impress in north London, the clause that allowed Spurs to sign him permanently has expired.

They have instead signed Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali in deals that cost a combined £185m.

It means Palhinha faces uncertainty over where he will be playing in the new season, although he doesn't seem to be short of interest.

Aston Villa are understood to have been in talks for the 31-year-old, who is keen to stay in England.



Newcastle United are also reportedly keen on Palhinha as a potential replacement for the seemingly Arsenal-bound Bruno Guimaraes.

Sports.title: New FIFA presidential candidate emerges as pressure grows on Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Victor Montagliani is emerging as a serious contender to rival Gianni Infantino at the next FIFA presidential election, talkSPORT understands.

The potential for the Canadian to become the new FIFA president was exclusively revealed on talkSPORT during the World Cup.



3 Infantino us under increased pressure as FIFA president Credit: Getty

CONCACAF president Montagliani wants to be the top chief at FIFA president one day, as talkSPORT revealed earlier this month, and is now considering whether to put his name forward ahead of the November 18 deadline.

Sources close to the 60-year-old have argued his immediate focus is on being re-elected as CONCACAF president, but it is common knowledge the Canadian has aspirations to be FIFA president one day.

He is now toying with either going head to head with Infantino or pushing for the FIFA president to quit, giving him a more open path.



Sources believe CONCACAF's emphatic rejection of Infantino's plans to sell a stake of FIFA to private investors was in part tactical to align with UEFA and potentially secure votes in the long-run.

It means 96 Member Federations, 41 from CONCACAF and 55 from UEFA, are all against Infantino, and could even block vote against him in the presidential election if a viable candidate emerges.



World Cup chaos

Infantino had already faced scrutiny following the conclusion of the World Cup, including concerns over his relationship with US president Donald Trump, before his controversial plans were revealed.

The FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal would see the football governing body's commercial and operational arms merge as part of an organisation funded by private equity.



All 211 Member Associations were given a $40million (£30m) payment incentive by Infantino to back the project by September 19.

However, there has been stiff opposition to the plans from UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC, and some of Infantino's closest allies at FIFA are understood to also be opposed.

Carlos Cordeiro, the president's senior adviser, has even quit his role in protest of the proposed sale of World Cup stakes.

3 Multiple candidates have been tipped to rival Infantino for the presidency Credit: AFP



It is clear UEFA would welcome a challenger to Infantino if he insists on standing even if FFE fails.

UEFA federations would also welcome Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi standing, but sources close to the Qatari businessman insist he has 'no ambition' to do so.

UEFA President Alexander Ceferin would be the most qualified name, but the Slovenian lawyer is understood to be willing to continue in his current role as UEFA President next Spring.

He had initially ruled out standing for a third full term until 2031, but is now willing to seek re-election if no other candidates step forward.



Ceferin is not looking to go head-to-head with Infantino despite clashing on issues on a number of occasions.

talkSPORT also understands senior officials within Bosnian, Norwegian, Swedish, German and Spanish football have all discussed backing other European candidates, including Legia owner Dariusz Mioduski.

3 The FFE plans have been given little to no support Credit: Getty

Should Al-Khelaifi choose not to stand, which is the current expectation, Poland would favour Mioduski as well.



Confederation of African Football president Patrice Motsepe is another name intent on being FIFA president one day.

The South African administrator is highly unlikely to go head-to-head with close ally Infantino, instead preferring to wait until 2031 in the hope of getting an endorsement during an election Infantino can't stand again in.

When do nominations to be the next FIFA president close?

And there appears to be no appetite to table a vote of no confidence against Infantino either despite it being toyed with at the last FIFA Congress.

Most federations will simply view the election itself as a vote of confidence, which is why a growing number of UEFA members are hoping to back another candidate to avoid Infantino winning a new term without a genuine debate.



Nominations for the next FIFA presidential election can be made up until November 18 with the election taking place on November 18 in Rabat, Morocco.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace star declares parents convinced him to snub summer switch to Saudi Arabia
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace star declares parents convinced him to snub summer switch to Saudi Arabia

Daichi Kamada has revealed how his parents helped to sway him from leaving Crystal Palace for Saudi Arabia.

Kamada looked set to leave Selhurst Park as a free agent this summer at the end of the two-year deal he signed in July 2024.

2 Kamada could have gone to Saudi Arabia, but will remain in London Credit: Getty

However, he has committed his future to the Palace by signing a new one-year deal to keep him at the club until 2027.

The 29-year-old has been a key part of the club's success during the past two seasons with FA Cup and Conference League triumphs.

Kamada did enough to attract interest from Saudi Arabia, where he could have been in line for a huge payday amid its lucrative finances.

But, after consultation with his parents, the midfielder opted not to move there and remain in south London.

Staying put

Speaking to TV Asahi Sports, via @Fooootest on X, he said: "Up until last winter, I had an offer from Saudi Arabia and was thinking about going there to secure my future.

"I thought my parents would be thrilled, but they told me, 'At this timing, absolutely do not go.'

"It was an enormous amount of money, so I figured they'd be delighted, but that was not the case at all."

Palace chairman Steve Parish was delighted to see Kamada extend his stay as he commented: "This is fantastic news for Crystal Palace. Over the last two years Daichi has made a great impact in the centre of midfield, as well as becoming a fans’ favourite on and off the pitch.

"I am delighted that he has turned down the many options he had to extend his stay in South London.

"Daichi will now have a well-earned break after his excellent World Cup and join us later in pre-season as we enter a busy Premier League and European season."

2 Kamada will stay at Palace for at least another season Credit: Getty

A new dawn at Selhurst

Palace are set to begin their first season under Pierre Sage, who has replaced Oliver Glasner as manager.

They will also make their Europa League debut, having qualified with their Conference League success in May.

Oscar Mingueza is their only summer signing so far following his free transfer from Celta Vigo.

However, they have banked £52million by selling Maxence Lacroix to Premier League rivals Chelsea.

Palace's pre-season schedule got underway with a 5-1 victory over Swindon Town before defeats to Bromley and Lens.

A 0-0 draw with Famalicao followed, with the Eagles then beating Al Ula 3-1 on Friday night.

Sports.title: Revealed: Amateur cricket cheat 'Clicky Ponting' used his notorious finger clicking hoax to get THREE batsmen out in title decider
Sports.content:
Do YOU have a story? Email tips@dailymail.com

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The amateur cricketer whose finger-clicking wicket deception has sparked a global cheating storm apparently once used the same trick to win his team a trophy in a title decider match, the Daily Mail can reveal.

Brian Devine – now known as 'Clicky Ponting' – seems to have hoodwinked umpires to get three opponent batsmen out in a key match in which his side needed a convincing victory to clinch a local league championship.

The proudest moment in Devine's amateur sporting career came when he led former club Pudsey St Lawrence to the Bradford Premier League second tier title in 2023.

The team, which is nicknamed the Saints, had to convincingly beat their oldest rivals Pudsey Congs in a 50-over derby match on the final day of the season if they were to win the trophy.

Devine, the team's captain, was hoping to go out on a high note as it was to be his last ever game for the club.

A day of high drama at their opponent's Amber Cars Britannia ground in the West Yorkshire market town ended in Pudsey St Lawrence winning the title with an emphatic eight wicket victory.

As skipper, Devine, 38, was seen proudly holding aloft the league championship trophy in photographs posted on the club's social media feeds.

But the newly unearthed footage – which was live-streamed at the time and has since been uncovered by the Mail – casts the result of the title-winning match into doubt.

The amateur cricketer whose finger-clicking wicket deception has sparked a global cheating storm apparently once used the same trick to win his team a trophy in a title decider match (pictured), the Daily Mail can reveal

Brian Devine (pictured), who is now known as 'Clicky Ponting', seems to have hoodwinked umpires to get three opponent batsmen out in a key match in which his side needed a convincing victory to clinch a local league championship

It shows Devine apparently attempting to mislead umpires with his finger clicking antics on a series of occasions – leading to wickets falling at crucial points in the game.

The Daily Mail can reveal that three bemused players from the opposing team were given out in almost identical circumstances – after balls flew past their bats at close proximity before landing in the gloves of the wicketkeeper.

Devine is clearly seen clicking his fingers in what appear to be carefully timed routines that mimicked the sound of a ball hitting the bat.

The Mail had already revealed earlier this week how Devine's clicky antics had been dated back a full five years to his days playing for Pudsey St Lawrence.

Now today's fresh revelations have led to calls for the club, which was founded in 1845, to be stripped of the title it won thanks to Devine in 2023.

Members of rival teams – who believe umpires have been routinely misled over a number of years – want the Bradford Premier League to mount a formal investigation.

One source told the Daily Mail: 'Our lads have been looking back at surviving film and score books and we have come to the conclusion that he's been at it for years.

'Young players will have lost opportunities because of this, match results will have undoubtedly been affected, and there is a good case for now stripping Pudsey St Lawrence of its 2023 title.'

The source added: 'Devine was a highly competitive and quite bumptious captain, and the bigger question is of course what club staff and his team-mates did or didn't know about his antics.'

The new revelations come just days after Devine was suspended for the 'foreseeable future' by his current club Saltburn CC over accusations he had used his clicking technique to trick umpires into wrongly giving batsmen out.

The club were placed under investigation by the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League following a complaint made in the aftermath of Saltburn's 159-run win over Norton in a Second XI Division Two match.

Video footage of the incident went viral online and has been reported around the globe – where commentators from England's biggest cricketing rivals including Australia have been leading the condemnation.

Devine – who is company secretary and financial manager of a livestock auction house – is yet to comment on the allegations.

The 2023 title-win proved third time lucky for Pudsey St Lawrence under Devine's captaincy after they had finished third in the table in 2021 and fourth in 2022.

One of the most venerable teams in club cricket, Pudsey St Lawrence has produced two of Yorkshire and England's greatest ever players – Herbert Sutcliffe, who averaged more than 60 in Test matches, and Sir Leonard Hutton, who scored 368 against Australia in 1938.

The new revelations come just days after Devine was suspended for the 'foreseeable future' by his current club Saltburn CC over accusations he had used his clicking technique in a Second XI Division Two match (pictured) against Norton Cricket Club last weekend

A complaint was made in the aftermath of Saltburn's 159-run win last Saturday. Video footage of the incident (pictured) later went viral online and has been reported around the globe

New Zealand stars Mark Greatbatch and Martin Crowe also spent time playing there.

The club has had a longstanding local rivalry with Pudsey Congs where former England pace bowler Matthew Hoggard started out.

There was great anticipation when the teams came face to face on the final day of the season in September 2023.

The Saints – who put out a team made up of a handful of senior cricketers playing alongside young 'homegrown talent' – went into the match knowing they needed a convincing win as two other teams in the league including the then-reigning champions could have overhauled them.

In the footage uncovered by the Daily Mail in which the entire match is shown, spectators sitting on deck chairs positioned behind the boundary can be seen watching on as the drama unfolded on a day of glorious sunshine.

After winning the toss, the home team elected to open the batting and there were 15 runs on the scoreboard when the first wicket fell in the ninth over of the match.

Devine, who was fielding at third slip, can be seen apparently preparing his clicking action as the bowler delivered the first three balls of his over without conceding any runs.

When the batsman takes a hefty swing at the fourth delivery, Devine flamboyantly clicked his fingers as the ball raced past into the wicketkeeper's gloves.

The captain enthusiastically appealed to the umpire along with his other teammates – and the batsman was given out having scored just seven runs.

The bemused-looking player momentarily remains at his crease before walking off towards the pavilion.

Just 16 minutes later, with the score at 31-1, a second player was dismissed in an almost identical way.

The batsman, who had scored one run, apparently nicked the ball while playing a forward defensive shot.

In the background, Devine can be seen carrying out his seemingly well-prepared manoeuvre before leading the appeals for a dismissal.

Again, the umpire raised his finger and the batsman trudged off with the score at 31-2.

It was not until the 36th over of the match that Devine was apparently able to utilise his unique talent again.

With the score at 117-5, he moved himself into the position of first slip.

Two balls later, with the wicketkeeper standing up to the wicket, Devine apparently clicked his fingers again as the ball went past the bat into the keeper's gloves.

The batsman, who had scored just one run, stepped back into his crease as Devine led noisy celebrations.

When the match official confirmed that the batsman had been caught out, the player momentarily stood his ground as he appeared to question the decision.

He is seen repeatedly shaking his head as he walked off the pitch – once again in apparent disbelief.

In the end, Pudsey Congs slumped to a disappointing 142 all out after just 42.5 overs of play.

Devine went on to open the batting for his team – facing the very first ball of the innings.

He was the second batsman to lose his wicket, scoring just four runs before he was caught out after clearly edging the ball into the hands of the wicketkeeper – leaving his team struggling at 25-2.

Despite the early setback, his team quickly turned things around and took a firm grip of the match.

They suffered no further loss of wickets as they raced to a winning total with 76 balls remaining.

The title-winning team were applauded enthusiastically by delighted supporters who rose to their feet after the winning runs were scored.

Further footage of a Bradford Premier League match in August 2021 has also come to light, leading to claims Devine began his cheating antics as long as five years ago.

Only a tiny number of matches were filmed at the time but statistics show that during the three seasons Devine captained Pudsey St Lawrence, this particular wicketkeeper took 96 catches – an average of 32 per year.

After his championship-winning exploits, Devine returned to Saltburn, his childhood club, the following season.

In the two years that followed his departure, the wicketkeeper in question took 22 and 15 catches respectively. So far this season, he's managed just five.

Club officials, however, insist they had never received a complaint from opponents over the cricketer's behaviour.

The Mail revealed earlier this week how Devine's clicky antics had been dated back a full five years to his days playing for Pudsey St Lawrence. Pictured: Footage from a Bradford Premier League match in August 2021, in which he can be seen repeatedly clicking his fingers

Martin Reed, Chairperson at Pudsey St Lawrence Cricket Club, told the Daily Mail: 'We were not aware of any issues with Mr Devine's behaviour during his time at the club, nor were concerns raised with us by other clubs or officials.

'Had we been made aware of any issues at the time we would have taken appropriate action.

'It is some time since Mr Devine left Pudsey St Lawrence and we are aware that the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League and Saltburn Cricket Club are currently investigating the matter.'

Sports.title: UEFA declares loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino's FIFA presidency: Pressure mounts on under-fire boss after disastrous World Cup plot as football chiefs look to overthrow him
Sports.content:
The FA and UEFA are leading the charge to depose Gianni Infantino as FIFA president after he scrapped the 'shabby, back-room deal' to sell stakes in the World Cup.

Pressure is mounting on the under-fire boss after his controversial plan to sell a £3.1billion stake in football's most coveted tournament to a group of private investors led by Josh Kushner - an extended relation of US President Donald Trump - collapsed on Friday night.

The scheme, which received wholesale opposition from football nations around the world, has seen scrutiny on Infantino's presidency intensify.

UEFA, European football's governing body, spearheaded calls condemning Infantino's plot and, in a lengthy statement released on Saturday morning, declared they had lost trust in his leadership.

UEFA said: 'UEFA welcomes FIFA's decision to withdraw its plan to sell a stake in its competitions – including the World Cup – into private hands.

'The proposal was unanimously rejected by UEFA's national associations and by many other federations and confederations of all sizes around the world, whose job it is to protect football.

'UEFA thanks all the fans, leagues, clubs, players, individuals, associations and confederations that opposed the scheme, alongside the many Prime Ministers, Heads of State and commentators who have demonstrated to the FIFA President that football is not for sale.

UEFA have lost confidence in shamed FIFA president Gianni Infantino after 'shabby, back-room deal' to sell stakes in the World Cup.

Gianni Infantino waves goodbye to his unilateral plans for private investment in FIFA with his presidency in jeopardy

Carlos Cordeiro (left) quit as an advisor to Gianni Infantino (centre) on Friday

'We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast-track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account,' the UEFA statement continued.

'It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

'When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA's Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA. You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA', before telling the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of FIFA is your money. It's not the money of the FIFA President. It's your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else'.

'On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back-room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through was anything but transparent.

'And with reserves standing at over $5bn, he has also failed to use associations' money for the benefit of the game.

'UEFA will begin work immediately with partners and stakeholders all over the world and right across the game to propose a new way of distributing resources through the existing FIFA Forward programme.

'We must start to use some of that money that is sat idle in FIFA's bank account to deliver the kick-start that the grassroots and the wider game need in each of the 211 countries of FIFA. But we don't need to sell off the family silver to pay for it.

'This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun.'

FIFA member nations could trigger a vote of no confidence to oust Infantino, who is seeking a fourth term in next year's elections. The threshold to initiate the process is 46 FIFA member associations; UEFA have 55 members.

A spokeswoman for the English FA backed UEFA's statement despite the association having initially supported Infantino's re-election bid.

'We fully support UEFA's position,' an FA spokeswoman said. 'It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.'

In the early hours of Saturday morning, Infantino abandoned his proposals to inject private equity into the operational and commercial aspects of FIFA tournaments.

His humiliating backtrack came thanks to the heroics of UEFA, CONCACAF, the AFC and two members of the FIFA hierarchy, who all took a stand against his divisive plans

The AFC, Asia's governing body, were the third and final confederation to reject Gianni Infantino's proposal. Their resistance made it clear he did not have the support to proceed, as opposing nations rose to a staggering 135 - 64 per cent of the FIFA membership.

With the controversy surrounding Infantino, member nations could trigger a vote of no confidence. The threshold to initiate the process is 46 FIFA member associations

The commendation followed CONCACAF's rejection on Thursday and came after UEFA announced a boycott of FIFA competitions. New Zealand Football also objected to the plans, despite the OFC delaying a continent-wide response.

Infantino said: 'The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

'And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

'Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.

'Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

'Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, and particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.'

The statement marked an embarrassing U-turn, less than 24 hours after he attempted to clarify his plans - blaming the media for misconstruing them.

One international football insider told Daily Mail Sport: 'UEFA's response is at the nuclear button end of the spectrum, which is impressive. We thought Infantino would survive the Trump refereeing intervention - but he has overreached this time.'

The proposal reached a terminal stage when Carlos Cordeiro, senior advisor to Gianni Infantino, announced his resignation from FIFA - becoming the first internal dissident.

Six hours later, FIFA's chief operating officer Kevin Lamour turned against the president - risking his job by criticising the plans and calling on nations to dethrone Infantino. Lamour admitted FIFA Forward Enterprise was the brainchild of 'one person' as he landed a critical blow to the FIFA president.

Infantino had hoped to create a new enterprise with significant investment from Joshua Kushner - brother of Jared, Donald Trump's son-in-law. Meanwhile, investment bank J.P. Morgan were advising on potential investors.

Democratic senator Ron Wyden, who leads an investigation into Jared Kushner, said on Friday: 'Soccer fans around the world are rightfully outraged by this scheme from Infantino and Joshua Kushner to turn the World Cup into just another commodity for private equity to buy up.

'It seems clear from the global backlash that this corrupt plan is unlikely to succeed, but it is just one of dozens of shady deals by Trump's family and close associates to get rich from the presidency.'

A significant number of FIFA members raised concerns from the initial leak of the plan, questioning how such thorough ideas could be developed unilaterally without prior consultation.

Despite FIFA maintaining throughout that there would be a proper consultation period, there were major questions about how that could be achieved when potential investors were already lined up.

UEFA accused FIFA of trying to bribe members with a £30million ($40million) incentive to approve Infantino's plan, with a September 19 deadline to respond to the offer.

Alongside UEFA's protest, sources told the Daily Mail Sport that CONCACAF nations believe he is losing or has already lost their confidence.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham believes Infantino's position is untenable and he is not alone.

Speaking to reporters in Sheffield on Friday, Burnham said: 'This was an outrageous suggestion. The idea that it could even be brought forward shows that, in my view, [he] is the wrong man to lead the organisation.'

Sepp Blatter, Infantino's predecessor, took to social media to renew his attacks on his successor by writing on Friday evening: 'FIFA is not a private equity fund. It is an association with statutes, regulations, and a fiduciary responsibility to protect the global game.

'If you sell football's crown jewels to private investors, you also sell part of the game – especially its soul. Money matters, but it must never become everything.'

The president of Jordan's Football Association - who ran against Infantino for president in 2016 - Ali Al Hussein argued that one of the issues facing FIFA's hierarchy was its secret ballot.

'With all the controversy surrounding FIFA, world football is facing a clear cut crisis in leadership just before an upcoming election,' Al Hussein wrote on social media.

'As someone who has been through this process before, I believe one thing needs to be done immediately: remove a secret ballot for Presidential elections!

'Every other decision including hosting the World Cup is now done openly, except - of course - for presidential elections. With a President who we elect every four years and a council that makes all the decisions, a transparent ballot is the only way to hold us as MA (member association) Presidents accountable in front of our own football fans, officials and players who elected us.

'At the same time it is protection for each and every MA who might be pressured to make a decision based on coercion behind closed doors as has happened in the past. But most importantly it will empower each and every MA on the most critical vote we have, the leadership of the biggest and most popular sport in the world and the direction it takes in the future.'

Al-Hussein was the runner-up in the contest to replace Blatter, receiving 88 votes (43 per cent of the votes), to Infantino's 115 (56 per cent).
